paper_summaries.title: Guidelines for the use and interpretation of assays for monitoring autophagy (4th edition)
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the standardization of methods for monitoring canonical and noncanonical autophagy across different organisms. The biological systems discussed include multicellular eukaryotes and general cellular models. Methods include various autophagy assays and genetic approaches targeting autophagy-related genes. The main contribution is providing updated guidelines for investigators to select and interpret appropriate techniques for evaluating autophagic processes.

paper_summaries.title: Organellomic gradients in the fourth dimension.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the temporal dimension of the organellome, encompassing the formation, maturation, functioning, and decay of organelles. The biological system is plant cells and tissues. Methods include organellomics tools for characterizing structural diversity and quantifying organelle abundance. The main contribution is highlighting how the temporal variability of the organellome influences plant phenotypic plasticity, polarity, and environmental resiliency.

paper_summaries.title: Phragmoplast navigator needs high IQ.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the mechanisms of phragmoplast navigation during plant cell division. The biological system is the plant cell phragmoplast. Methods are not clearly specified in abstract. The main contribution is discussing the regulatory and navigational requirements for proper phragmoplast guidance.

paper_summaries.title: Plant Cytokinesis: Terminology for Structures and Processes.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the terminology used to describe the structures and processes of plant cytokinesis, specifically focusing on the phragmoplast. The biological systems are land plants and Charophyte algae. Methods are not clearly specified in abstract. The main contribution is proposing a standardized lexicon for plant cytokinesis to facilitate knowledge transfer and clarify complex signaling and structural networks.

paper_summaries.title: Regulation of cytokinetic machinery in plants.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the regulation of the cytokinetic machinery, focusing on cell plate biogenesis and phragmoplast expansion. The biological system is dividing plant cells. Methods are not clearly specified in abstract. The main contribution is summarizing the key signaling pathways that coordinate microtubule organization, vesicle trafficking, membrane remodeling, and oligosaccharide deposition during plant cytokinesis.

paper_summaries.title: An overview of plant division-plane orientation.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the mechanisms controlling the positioning and orientation of the new cell wall during plant cell division. The biological system is plant cells. Methods include shape-based computational models and mutant analyses. The main contribution is reviewing evidence that the proteins required for division-plane establishment are distinct from those needed for its maintenance.

paper_summaries.title: Redundant mechanisms in division plane positioning.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the redundant mechanisms that contribute to the maintenance of proper division plane orientation in plant cells. The biological system is plant cells. Methods are not clearly specified in abstract. The main contribution is categorizing these redundancies into temporal, genetic, and synthetic types to provide insight into current models of division plane orientation.

paper_summaries.title: Plant Cytokinesis: Terminology for Structures and Processes.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the terminology used to describe the structures and processes of plant cytokinesis, specifically focusing on the phragmoplast. The biological systems are land plants and Charophyte algae. Methods are not clearly specified in abstract. The main contribution is proposing a standardized lexicon for plant cytokinesis to facilitate knowledge transfer and clarify complex signaling and structural networks.

paper_summaries.title: Cell biology of primary cell wall synthesis in plants.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the trafficking and assembly of cell wall components during diffuse growth and cytokinesis. The biological system is plant cells. Methods are not clearly specified in abstract. The main contribution is detailing how the cytoskeleton organizes the addition of new cell wall material and how polysaccharides and enzymes are trafficked to the correct locations by motor proteins.

paper_summaries.title: Hyphal homing, fusion and mycelial interconnectedness.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the processes of hyphal homing and fusion that lead to interconnected mycelial networks. The biological system is fungal mycelia. Methods are not clearly specified in abstract. The main contribution is examining the cellular mechanisms underlying the formation of interconnected fungal networks.

paper_summaries.title: The B73 maize genome: complexity, diversity, and dynamics.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the draft nucleotide sequence and genomic structure of the 2.3-gigabase maize genome. The biological system is Zea mays (B73 maize). Methods include genome sequencing, gene prediction, transposable element analysis, and methylation profiling. The main contribution is reporting the placement of over 32,000 genes and detailing how transposable elements and uneven gene losses shaped the genome's complexity and centromere composition.

paper_summaries.title: Circadian coordination of cellular processes and abiotic stress responses.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the role of the circadian clock in synchronizing environmental signals with internal biological processes and stress responses. The biological system is Arabidopsis. Methods are not clearly specified in abstract. The main contribution is highlighting the circadian regulation of alternative splicing, noncoding RNAs, reactive oxygen species, calcium signaling, and the gating of temperature stress responses.

paper_summaries.title: Investigating Circadian Gating of Temperature Responsive Genes.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies experimental designs for investigating the circadian gating of temperature-responsive genes. The biological systems are Arabidopsis thaliana and bread wheat (Triticum aestivum). Methods include gating experiments under constant conditions and light-dark cycles, utilizing heat (37°C) and cold (4°C) treatments. The main contribution is describing specific laboratory protocols to dissect the contribution of the time of day and circadian clock to dynamic stress-responsive gene expression.

paper_summaries.title: Interaction between the Circadian Clock and Regulators of Heat Stress Responses in Plants.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the interactions between the circadian clock and heat stress regulatory pathways. The biological system is plants. Methods are not clearly specified in abstract. The main contribution is reviewing how rhythmic transcription factors coordinate appropriate responses to temperature stress and how heat stress impacts clock-controlled gene regulation.

paper_summaries.title: Time of day and genotype sensitivity adjust molecular responses to temperature stress in sorghum.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the impact of time of day and genetic background on gene expression dynamics under temperature stress. The biological system is sorghum. Methods include gene expression profiling and temperature stress assays. The main contribution is demonstrating that time of day strongly influences temperature stress responses, particularly in thermo-tolerant genotypes, and identifying specific rhythmic genes like Ca2+-binding EF-hand proteins involved in this regulation.

paper_summaries.title: Unconventional Protein Secretion in Plants.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies unconventional protein secretion (UPS) pathways that bypass canonical secretion routes or involve leaderless proteins. The biological system is plant cells. Methods include vesicle proteomics and chemical genomics. The main contribution is discussing the correlation between UPS induction and pathogenesis or stress responses, and highlighting novel technologies for dissecting these secretion pathways.

paper_summaries.title: Editorial: Coordination of plant endomembrane system with developmental signals and environmental stimuli.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the coordination of the plant endomembrane system with developmental and environmental cues. The biological system is plants. Methods are not clearly specified in abstract. The main contribution is introducing a collection of studies focused on how the plant endomembrane system responds to various internal and external signals.

paper_summaries.title: Plant Cytokinesis: Terminology for Structures and Processes.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the terminology used to describe the structures and processes of plant cytokinesis, specifically focusing on the phragmoplast. The biological systems are land plants and Charophyte algae. Methods are not clearly specified in abstract. The main contribution is proposing a standardized lexicon for plant cytokinesis to facilitate knowledge transfer and clarify complex signaling and structural networks.

paper_summaries.title: Editorial: Regulation of and by the Plant Cell Wall.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the regulatory mechanisms related to the plant cell wall. The biological system is plants. Methods are not clearly specified in abstract. The main contribution is providing an editorial overview of current research on the regulation of and by the plant cell wall.

paper_summaries.title: The Plant Trans-Golgi Network: Not Just a Matter of Distinction.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the role of the trans-Golgi network as a major sorting station in plant cells. The biological system is plants. Methods are not clearly specified in abstract. The main contribution is describing the plant trans-Golgi network's function in sorting Golgi-derived cargo and receiving recycled material from endocytosis.

paper_summaries.title: Addressing noise in co-expression network construction.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the impact of noise and confounding variables on the construction of gene co-expression networks (GCNs) from large transcriptome datasets. The computational system involves transcriptome profiles and network models. Methods include the Knowledge Independent Network Construction toolkit and statistical testing for context-specific GCNs (csGCNs). The main contribution is demonstrating that up to 97% of GCN edges can be misleading in multivariable datasets and reviewing workflows to address these confounding variables.

paper_summaries.title: A chromosome-scale assembly for 'd'Anjou' pear.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the generation of a fully phased chromosome-scale genome assembly for the European pear cultivar 'd'Anjou'. The biological system is Pyrus communis 'd'Anjou'. Methods include PacBio HiFi sequencing, Dovetail Omni-C reads, RNA-seq, and comparative genomics. The main contribution is resolving the pear genome into 17 chromosomes per haplotype, annotating nearly 45,000 genes per haplotype, and detecting signatures of a shared whole-genome duplication event with apple.

paper_summaries.title: High-density multi-population consensus genetic linkage map for peach.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the development of a high-density consensus genetic linkage map for peach using multiple mapping populations. The biological system is peach (Prunus persica). Methods include the 9K SNP peach array, MergeMap, LPmerge, genetic linkage mapping, and QTL mapping. The main contribution is constructing a consensus linkage map containing 3,092 molecular markers across eight linkage groups, providing a valuable tool for QTL identification and comparative genetic studies in Rosaceae.

paper_summaries.title: GEMmaker: process massive RNA-seq datasets on heterogeneous computational infrastructure.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the development of a workflow for quantifying gene expression from massive RNA-seq datasets across diverse computational environments. The computational system involves local, cluster, and cloud infrastructures. Methods include the GEMmaker Nextflow workflow, containerized software, and RNA-seq alignment and quantification tools. The main contribution is introducing GEMmaker, a scalable and reproducible tool that processes thousands of RNA-seq samples without exceeding available data storage.

paper_summaries.title: A Haplotype-resolved, Chromosome-scale Genome for Malus domestica Borkh. 'WA 38'.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the assembly and annotation of a haplotype-phased, chromosomal-level genome for the 'WA 38' apple cultivar (Cosmic Crisp). The biological system is Malus domestica 'WA 38'. Methods include short and long read sequencing, k-mer based assembly, and containerized software workflows. The main contribution is providing the first fully phased pome fruit genome, separating chromosomes into 'Honeycrisp' and 'Enterprise' originated haplomes, and sharing a reproducible assembly workflow.

paper_summaries.title: CtBP1/2 oligomerization promotes G9a-Mediated transcriptional repression.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the structural basis of the interaction between corepressors CtBP1/2 and the histone methyltransferase G9a in transcriptional repression. The biological system includes colorectal cancer cell models. Using crystallographic and biochemical analyses, the study reveals that CtBP1/2 tetramerization enhances G9a catalytic activity and H3K9me2 deposition, which promotes colorectal cancer cell proliferation.

paper_summaries.title: Slipknot-gauged mechanical transmission and robotic operation.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper investigates a slipknot-based mechanical transmission mechanism for controlling force in human and robotic systems. The study utilizes topological design and surgical repair models to evaluate force delivery. The main contribution demonstrates that slipknot tying and release can encode force with 95.4% consistency, improving surgical knotting precision and tissue healing without the need for additional sensors.

paper_summaries.title: DDX6 undergoes phase separation to modulate metabolic plasticity and chemoresistance.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper examines the role of DEAD-box helicase 6 (DDX6) and liquid-liquid phase separation in acute myeloid leukemia (AML) tumorigenesis. The researchers utilized in vitro and in vivo CRISPR screenings targeting RNA-binding proteins. The study finds that DDX6 knockout disrupts processing body assembly, leading to the degradation of BCAT1 mRNA, which reprograms amino acid metabolism and sensitizes AML cells to chemotherapy.

paper_summaries.title: Pharmacological inhibition of miR-126 enhances venetoclax activity in acute myeloid leukemia.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the role of microRNA-126 in maintaining leukemic stem cell function through the regulation of mitochondrial metabolism in acute myeloid leukemia. The research employs patient-derived xenograft models, venetoclax, and a CpG-conjugated anti-miR-126 oligonucleotide. The main contribution shows that inhibiting miR-126 disrupts BCL-2-dependent fatty acid oxidation and mitochondrial fusion, synergizing with venetoclax to prolong survival.

paper_summaries.title: Metformin Administration Protects Against Deltoid Tendon Damage Through Activation of Notch Signaling.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper investigates the protective effects of metformin against diabetic tendinopathy. The biological systems studied include patient data, cultured tenocytes, and tendon tissues from diabetic mice and aged monkeys. The study reveals that metformin administration reduces tendon damage and improves tendon fiber structure by upregulating the Notch signaling effector gene HES1.

paper_summaries.title: Cardiogenic control of affective behavioural state.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the influence of heart rate on anxiety-like behavior to test the flow of interoceptive information from the body to the brain. The biological system is freely moving mice. Using a noninvasive optogenetic pacemaker, wearable micro-LED harness, whole-brain activity screening, and electrophysiology, the study demonstrates that optically evoked tachycardia enhances anxiety in risky contexts via the posterior insular cortex.

paper_summaries.title: Three-dimensional genome structures of single diploid human cells.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper develops a method to reconstruct the 3D genome structures of single diploid human cells. The biological systems analyzed are a lymphoblastoid cell line and primary blood cells. Utilizing a single-cell chromatin conformation capture method called Dip-C, which combines transposon-based whole-genome amplification and haplotype imputation algorithms, the study reveals that different cell types display statistically distinct genome structures.

paper_summaries.title: Single-cell whole-genome analyses by Linear Amplification via Transposon Insertion (LIANTI).
paper_summaries.summary: This paper introduces an improved single-cell whole-genome amplification method for detecting copy-number and single-nucleotide variations. The computational and biological system involves single human cells. Using Linear Amplification via Transposon Insertion (LIANTI) and kindred cell sequencing, the study achieves kilobase-resolution micro-CNV detection and maps the genome-wide distribution of UV-induced mutations.

paper_summaries.title: Changes in genome architecture and transcriptional dynamics progress independently of sensory experience during post-natal brain development.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper investigates the post-natal dynamics of the single-cell transcriptome and 3D genome in the developing mammalian brain. The biological system is the developing mouse cortex and hippocampus. Using MALBAC-DT and Dip-C methods, the study generates a multi-omic atlas showing that 3D genome rewiring in neurons correlates with gene expression modules and progresses independently of sensory experience.
methods_or_data: MALBAC-DT (multiple annealing and looping-based amplification cycles for digital transcriptomics)

paper_summaries.title: Mapping the cellular etiology of schizophrenia and complex brain phenotypes.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper maps the specific cell types involved in the etiology of schizophrenia and other complex brain phenotypes. The study integrates genome-wide and brain-wide genetics and transcriptomics datasets. The main contribution identifies specific neuronal associations for psychiatric disorders, such as somatostatin interneurons, contrasting with immune cell associations found for multiple sclerosis and Alzheimer's disease.

paper_summaries.title: Cohesin Loss Eliminates All Loop Domains.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper explores the effects of cohesin degradation on 3D genome organization and gene regulation. The biological system involves human genomic intervals. While specific methods are not clearly specified in abstract, the study demonstrates that cohesin loss eliminates all loop domains without affecting compartment domains or histone marks, causing superenhancers to co-localize and affect nearby gene regulation.

paper_summaries.title: Histone H1 loss drives lymphoma by disrupting 3D chromatin architecture.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper investigates the pathogenic role of linker histone H1 mutations in B cell lymphomas. The biological system includes mouse models and B cell lymphomas. Using epigenetic profiling and genomic architectural analysis, the study shows that H1 loss causes 3D genome decompaction, epigenetic reprogramming via H3K36me2 gain and H3K27me3 loss, and derepression of stem cell genes to drive malignant transformation.

paper_summaries.title: Biophysicists' outstanding response to Covid-19.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper discusses the response of the biophysics community to the Covid-19 pandemic. The biological or computational system is not clearly specified in abstract. Methods or data are not clearly specified in abstract. The main contribution highlights the efforts and contributions of biophysicists during the global health crisis.

paper_summaries.title: Machine learning tools advance biophysics.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper discusses the advancement of biophysics through the application of machine learning tools. The biological or computational system is not clearly specified in abstract. Methods or data are not clearly specified in abstract. The main contribution highlights the impact of computational and machine learning approaches on biophysical research.

paper_summaries.title: Structural insights into the cooperative nucleosome recognition and chromatin opening by FOXA1 and GATA4.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the structural mechanisms of cooperative nucleosome recognition and chromatin opening by the pioneer factors FOXA1 and GATA4. The biological system focuses on the N1 nucleosome in the enhancer of the ALB1 gene. Using cryo-electron microscopy, in vivo DNA editing, and bioinformatics analyses, the study reveals that FOXA1 repositions the N1 nucleosome to enhance GATA4 binding, opening chromatin by bending linker DNA.

paper_summaries.title: Autobiography of Dave Thirumalai.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper presents an autobiographical account of the author's career. The biological or computational system is not clearly specified in abstract. Methods or data are not clearly specified in abstract. The main contribution is a historical overview of the author's professional life.

paper_summaries.title: Molecular mechanisms of steric pressure generation and membrane remodeling by disordered proteins.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper investigates the molecular mechanisms by which intrinsically disordered proteins generate steric pressure to remodel cellular membranes. The biological system involves the intrinsically disordered domain of the endocytic protein AP180 on membrane surfaces. Using a Förster resonance energy transfer (FRET)-based sensor, the study finds that disordered domains generate substantial entropic and electrostatic steric pressure that is invariant with molecular weight at constant membrane coverage.

paper_summaries.title: High-throughput mass spectrometry maps the sepsis plasma proteome and differences in patient response.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper maps the plasma proteome of patients with sepsis to understand pathophysiology and patient response differences. The study analyzes 2612 plasma samples and paired leukocyte transcriptomic data from 1611 patients. Using high-throughput liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry, the research identifies proteins, pathways, and coexpression modules related to sepsis etiology, clinical phenotypes, and severity.

paper_summaries.title: Systemic 4-1BB stimulation augments extrafollicular memory B cell formation and recall responses during Plasmodium infection.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper examines the effect of an agonistic antibody targeting 4-1BB on memory B cell formation during experimental Plasmodium infection. The biological system is a mouse model of malaria. Utilizing single-cell RNA sequencing and ATAC sequencing, the study shows that systemic 4-1BB stimulation enhances humoral memory recall and protection from reinfection via IL-9R signaling in B cells.

paper_summaries.title: Pleural fluid proteomics from patients with pleural infection shows signatures of diverse neutrophilic responses: The Oxford Pleural Infection Endotyping Study (TORPIDS-2).
paper_summaries.summary: This paper analyzes the biological endotypes of pleural infection using pleural fluid proteomics. The study utilizes 80 pleural fluid samples from a prospective study. Using unlabelled mass spectrometry, unsupervised hierarchical clustering, and 16S rRNA next-generation sequencing, the research reveals that pleural infections exhibit diverse neutrophil-mediated immunity, glycolysis, and pentose phosphate activation responses that correlate with specific microbial profiles.

paper_summaries.title: SARS-CoV-2 infection induces a long-lived pro-inflammatory transcriptional profile.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper investigates the long-term effects of SARS-CoV-2 infection on the immune system's transcriptional profile. The biological system includes circulating T, B, and NK cells and monocytes from three independent patient cohorts. Using targeted single-cell multiomics and bulk transcriptomics, the study discovers a prolonged, NF-κB-driven pro-inflammatory gene expression signature that persists for months after symptom onset.

paper_summaries.title: Natural Killer cells demonstrate distinct eQTL and transcriptome-wide disease associations, highlighting their role in autoimmunity.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper performs expression quantitative trait locus (eQTL) mapping of Natural Killer cells to understand their role in autoimmunity. The biological system involves negatively selected Natural Killer cells from 245 healthy Europeans. Using transcriptomic data and transcriptome-wide association studies across five autoimmune diseases, the research identifies NK cell-specific eQTLs and novel master-regulatory regions impacting trans gene networks.

paper_summaries.title: Fast and sensitive protein alignment using DIAMOND.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the computational bottleneck of aligning sequencing reads against protein reference databases in metagenomics and evolutionary projects. The biological system involves computational sequence alignment of short reads. Using the DIAMOND algorithm based on double indexing, the study compares performance against the gold standard BLASTX. The main contribution is the introduction of DIAMOND, an open-source algorithm that is 20,000 times faster than BLASTX on short reads while maintaining a similar degree of sensitivity.

paper_summaries.title: Neanderthal behaviour, diet, and disease inferred from ancient DNA in dental calculus.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies Neanderthal ecology, diet, behavior, and disease using ancient DNA preserved in calcified dental plaque. The biological system is the Neanderthal oral microbiota and dental calculus from specimens found in Belgium and Spain. Methods include shotgun-sequencing of ancient DNA, metagenomic data analysis, and microbial genome assembly. The study characterizes regional dietary differences, identifies evidence of self-medication, and reconstructs a 48,000-year-old draft genome of the archaeal commensal Methanobrevibacter oralis.

paper_summaries.title: DIAMOND + MEGAN Microbiome Analysis.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the taxonomic and functional composition of microbiomes using DNA sequencing technologies. The computational system involves microbiome DNA sequencing data aligned against protein reference databases like NCBI-nr. The study utilizes the DIAMOND+MEGAN pipeline on publicly available short-read and long-read datasets. The main contribution is illustrating how to apply this pipeline to perform taxonomic and functional binning for interactive microbiome analysis.

paper_summaries.title: Normalising phylogenetic networks.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the simplification of complex rooted phylogenetic networks inferred from genomic data. The computational system focuses on mathematical models of species' evolutionary relationships. Methods involve mathematical transformation algorithms based on the visible vertices in the original network. The main contribution is the description and implementation of a natural method to transform tangled rooted phylogenetic networks into simpler canonical networks with desirable mathematical and computational properties.

paper_summaries.title: NeighborNet: improved algorithms and implementation.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies computational improvements to the NeighborNet method, which is used to construct phylogenetic networks for visualizing distance data. The system involves computational phylogenetics and distance data visualization. Methods include algorithmic refinements for computing circular ordering and estimating split weights. The main contribution is presenting a simplified formulation for the algorithm's first step and providing the first technical description of the split weight estimation step.

paper_summaries.title: Contamination in Low Microbial Biomass Microbiome Studies: Issues and Recommendations.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the impact of contaminant DNA and cross-contamination on the interpretation of microbiome data. The biological system focuses on low microbial biomass samples analyzed via next-generation sequencing. Methods include literature review and the development of the 'RIDE' checklist. The main contribution is identifying key measures to reduce contamination impacts and proposing minimal experimental criteria to improve the validity of low microbial biomass research.

paper_summaries.title: Neanderthal behaviour, diet, and disease inferred from ancient DNA in dental calculus.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies Neanderthal ecology, diet, behavior, and disease using ancient DNA preserved in calcified dental plaque. The biological system is the Neanderthal oral microbiota and dental calculus from specimens found in Belgium and Spain. Methods include shotgun-sequencing of ancient DNA, metagenomic data analysis, and microbial genome assembly. The study characterizes regional dietary differences, identifies evidence of self-medication, and reconstructs a 48,000-year-old draft genome of the archaeal commensal Methanobrevibacter oralis.

paper_summaries.title: Microbiome ownership for Indigenous peoples.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the ethical issues and concept of microbiome ownership in research involving Indigenous populations. The biological system is the human microbiome of Indigenous peoples. Methods are not clearly specified in abstract, but involve ethical and conceptual analysis. The main contribution is arguing that microbiome ownership represents an opportunity for Indigenous peoples to steward and protect their resident microbial communities throughout the research process.

paper_summaries.title: Off the beaten track: Understudied microbes and their potential.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies fundamental biological questions addressed through the use of unconventional microbial models. The biological system involves diverse, understudied, and non-pathogenic microbes. Methods are not clearly specified in abstract. The main contribution is highlighting the work of six scientists who utilize these unconventional microbial models to explore fundamental biology.

paper_summaries.title: Guidelines for preventing and reporting contamination in low-biomass microbiome studies.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies strategies to mitigate and report contamination in low microbial biomass environments. The biological systems include human tissues, the atmosphere, plant seeds, treated drinking water, hyper-arid soils, and the deep subsurface. Methods involve marker gene and metagenomic analyses using DNA-based sequencing. The main contribution is a Consensus Statement that outlines minimal standards and workflows for reducing, identifying, and reporting contamination and cross-contamination in low-biomass microbiome studies.

paper_summaries.title: Mapping the proteo-genomic convergence of human diseases.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the genetic regulation of proteins to better understand disease etiology and develop therapies. The biological system involves human plasma proteins and their associated genetic variants. Methods include genome-wide association studies (GWAS) to create a cis-anchored gene-protein-disease map using 10,674 genetic associations for 3892 plasma proteins. The main contribution is providing a proteo-genomic framework of 1859 connections that highlights cross-disease biological convergence and establishes the value of cis-protein variants for annotating causal disease genes.

paper_summaries.title: Genome-wide association analysis and Mendelian randomization proteomics identify drug targets for heart failure.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies novel genetic determinants and druggable protein targets for heart failure. The biological system is the human cardiovascular system, analyzed across over 90,000 heart failure cases and more than 1 million controls. Methods include genome-wide association studies (GWAS), Mendelian randomization, genetic cis-only colocalization analyses, and blood protein quantitative loci. The main contribution is identifying 39 genome-wide significant heart failure risk variants and highlighting seven proteins as potential targets for primary prevention interventions.

paper_summaries.title: Metabolomic profiles predict individual multidisease outcomes.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the use of metabolomic profiles for risk stratification and early identification of 24 common conditions. The biological system involves 168 circulating metabolic markers in humans. Methods include nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy and neural network models trained on data from 117,981 UK Biobank participants. The main contribution is demonstrating that NMR-derived metabolomic states, combined with age and sex, equal or outperform established clinical predictors for 10-year outcome prediction across multiple diseases.

paper_summaries.title: Systemic proteome adaptions to 7-day complete caloric restriction in humans.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the systemic proteomic adaptations to extreme caloric restriction in humans. The biological system is the human plasma proteome and multi-organ response during a 7-day water-only fast in 12 volunteers. Methods include temporal trajectory analysis of approximately 3,000 plasma proteins and proteogenomic approaches. The main contribution is revealing nine distinct proteomic response profiles, highlighting significant non-metabolic adaptations such as changes in brain-specific extracellular matrix proteins, and estimating health consequences for 212 responding proteins.

paper_summaries.title: Proteomic signatures improve risk prediction for common and rare diseases.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the use of objective plasma protein biomarkers to predict the 10-year incidence of 218 common and rare diseases. The biological system is the human plasma proteome, analyzed in 41,931 individuals from the UK Biobank Pharma Proteomics Project. Methods include measuring ~3,000 plasma proteins, single-cell RNA sequencing, and developing sparse prediction models. The main contribution is showing that sparse plasma protein signatures of 5 to 20 proteins outperform basic clinical information and standard clinical assays for predicting the onset of numerous pathologically diverse diseases.
methods_or_data: UK Biobank Pharma Proteomics Project data

paper_summaries.title: Arresting Evolution.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper reviews strategies to stop or slow unwanted evolution, which can lead to drug resistance or unreliable engineered cells. The study examines general biological systems, including pathogens and engineered organisms, using literature review and population genetics concepts. Methods include population genetics models and genome editing techniques. The main contribution is a classification of existing methods for arresting evolution and a discussion of how genome editing enables new approaches to limit evolutionary processes.

paper_summaries.title: Engineering insects from the endosymbiont out.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper examines the genetic engineering of bacterial symbionts to understand and manipulate insect-microbe associations. The biological system comprises insects and their endosymbiont or gut bacterial species. Methods discussed include genetic modification techniques for symbionts. The main contribution is a synthesis of recent studies that use symbiont engineering to influence insect biology, highlighting applications in pest control and pollinator health.

paper_summaries.title: pLannotate: engineered plasmid annotation.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper presents the development of pLannotate, an open-source web server designed to comprehensively annotate functional elements in engineered plasmids. The computational system utilizes large databases of genetic parts and proteins alongside a custom filtering algorithm. The main contribution is a tool that accurately identifies both complete and fragmented genetic features, providing graphical maps and provenance for each prediction to improve plasmid design and verification.

paper_summaries.title: Honey bee functional genomics using symbiont-mediated RNAi.
paper_summaries.summary: This study develops a method to induce sustained RNA interference in honey bees by engineering the gut bacterium Snodgrassella alvi. The biological system involves honey bees and their bacterial symbionts. Methods include Golden Gate assembly of dsRNA expression plasmids, bacterial colonization, and qRT-PCR to measure gene expression. The main contribution is the establishment of the FUGUES protocol, which achieves 50-75% knockdown of targeted host genes throughout the bee body.

paper_summaries.title: Evolutionary loss of an antibiotic efflux pump increases Pseudomonas aeruginosa quorum sensing mediated virulence in vivo.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper investigates the mechanisms by which the evolutionary loss of the mexEFoprN antibiotic efflux pump increases the virulence of Pseudomonas aeruginosa. The biological system includes clinical isolates of P. aeruginosa from cystic fibrosis and acute respiratory infections. The study utilizes genome sequencing, RNA-seq, metabolomics, genetic manipulation, and in vivo infection models. The main contribution is demonstrating that efflux pump inactivating mutations elevate quorum sensing-driven expression of virulence factors, thereby increasing pathogenesis.

paper_summaries.title: Keeping membraneless organelles apart.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the mechanisms involved in keeping membraneless organelles apart. The biological system focuses on cellular membraneless organelles. Methods and data types are not clearly specified in abstract. The main contribution relates to understanding the spatial separation and maintenance of these biomolecular condensates.

paper_summaries.title: Structure-Function Properties in Disordered Condensates.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper investigates how the structural properties of disordered biomolecular condensates influence client molecule recruitment and functionality. The study uses a model system composed of poly-SUMO and poly-SIM proteins. Specific experimental or computational methods are not clearly specified in abstract. The main contribution is demonstrating that the filamentous structure of the network constrains scaffold stoichiometries and client binding sites, leading to a tunable, nonmonotonic client binding response.

paper_summaries.title: Phosphorylation enables allosteric control of a viral condensate.
paper_summaries.summary: This study examines how sequence diversity in the intrinsically disordered protein NSP5 affects the formation of replicative condensates in species A rotaviruses. The biological system is the rotavirus NSP5 protein and its liquid-liquid phase separation behavior. Methods include machine learning, recombinant virus assays, and hydrogen-deuterium exchange mass spectrometry. The main contribution is discovering that phosphorylation acts as an allosteric switch to nucleate phase separation in low-propensity viral strains.

paper_summaries.title: Distinct growth regimes of α-synuclein amyloid elongation.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper assesses the elongation kinetics of α-synuclein amyloid fibers to understand how growth rates depend on instantaneous monomer concentration. The biological system is the α-synuclein protein, whose aggregation is linked to Parkinson's disease. The study utilizes Thioflavin T fluorescence, solution-state NMR spectroscopy, and mathematical modeling. The main contribution is the identification of distinct growth regimes, including a previously undetected fast disordered elongation phase at high monomer concentrations.

paper_summaries.title: Sequence-encoded interactions program internal condensate architecture.
paper_summaries.summary: This study investigates how specific molecular interactions establish the internal multiphase architecture of cellular condensates. The systems analyzed include a programmable DNA system and RNA-peptide systems. The research employs associative polymer modeling and programmable DNA assembly. The main contribution is demonstrating that overcoming a critical interaction energy threshold triggers internal demixing, allowing the engineering of condensates with up to four coexisting phases exhibiting vastly different viscosities.

cards.human_proposal_title: Energetic Origins of Connectivity within Protein Interaction Networks

paper_summaries.title: Recent developments in cystic fibrosis drug discovery: where are we today?
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the limitations of current CFTR modulator therapies and emerging strategies for cystic fibrosis drug discovery. The biological system is human cystic fibrosis, specifically focusing on rare CFTR variants. Methods and data types are not clearly specified in the abstract, as it is an expert review of theratyping and small molecule identification. The main contribution is highlighting the critical need to optimize testing strategies for ultra-rare variants and addressing barriers to therapeutic access for minority and underprivileged populations.

paper_summaries.title: Disease-linked supertrafficking of a potassium channel.
paper_summaries.summary: This study investigates whether gain-of-function (GOF) mutations in the KCNQ1 potassium channel induce cardiac arrhythmia by increasing the amount of channel reaching the cell surface. The system studied is the human KCNQ1 voltage-gated potassium channel. Methods include whole-cell electrophysiology recordings and surface trafficking assays. The main contribution is demonstrating that the R231C mutation causes a fivefold increase in plasma membrane levels due to enhanced translocon-mediated integration and folding, which offsets reduced single-channel activity to produce a GOF phenotype.

paper_summaries.title: Unifying perspectives on the activity and genotypic targeting of pharmacological chaperones.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper explores the factors that shape the potency and genotypic targeting of pharmacological chaperones used to treat protein misfolding diseases. The system involves misfolded pathogenic protein variants and their cellular contexts. Methods and data types are not clearly specified in the abstract, as it provides a theoretical framework and literature review. The main contribution is providing a unifying perspective on how the thermodynamic coupling between ligand binding and protein folding influences the variant-specific effects of pharmacochaperones.

paper_summaries.title: Deep Receptor Scanning Reveals General Sequence Constraints on GPCR Biosynthesis.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the sequence and structural constraints governing the biosynthesis and expression of G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs). The system comprises 766 human GPCRs and 174 splice variants expressed in a recombinant pool of HEK293T cells. Methods include a "deep receptor scanning" platform, transcript abundance quantification, translational efficiency assays, plasma membrane expression assays, and machine learning. The main contribution is the introduction of an experimental and informatic platform that quantitatively characterizes GPCR expression and identifies specific structural features modulating receptor biosynthesis.

paper_summaries.title: Regulators of Viral Frameshifting: More Than RNA Influences Translation Events.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper examines the mechanisms and regulatory elements of programmed ribosomal frameshifting (PRF) in both host and viral translation. The biological systems discussed include viral, bacterial, archaeal, and eukaryotic translation machineries. Methods and data types are not clearly specified in the abstract, as it is a review of recent literature. The main contribution is summarizing the recent identification of novel cis and trans elements that regulate PRF beyond the traditional slippery heptanucleotide and RNA pseudoknot motifs.

paper_summaries.title: Inference of Gene Regulatory Network from Single-Cell Transcriptomic Data Using pySCENIC.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper describes the implementation and application of a pipeline for inferring cell-specific gene regulatory networks (GRNs) from single-cell RNA sequencing data. The computational system is the pySCENIC Python pipeline applied to single-cell transcriptomes. Methods include single-cell RNA-seq data analysis, co-expression-based target identification (GRNBoost2 and GENIE3), and transcription factor-motif enrichment analysis. The main contribution is providing a fast, efficient tool to map transcription factors to GRNs and score regulon activity across diverse cell types.

paper_summaries.title: CD2 expressing innate lymphoid and T cells are critical effectors of immunopathogenesis in hidradenitis suppurativa.
paper_summaries.summary: This study investigates the role of CD2-expressing innate lymphocytes and T cells in the immunopathogenesis of hidradenitis suppurativa (HS). The biological system is human HS lesional skin and ex vivo skin explant cultures. Methods include ex vivo explant cultures, monoclonal antibody blockade (anti-CD2), cytokine/chemokine secretion assays, inflammatory gene signature analysis, and miRNA profiling. The main contribution is demonstrating that a network of CD2+ NKT and NK cells interacting with CD58+ keratinocytes and fibroblasts drives HS inflammation, and that blocking this interaction attenuates the inflammatory response.

paper_summaries.title: Cdk5 mediates rotational force-induced brain injury.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the mechanisms by which rotational injuries mediate neuronal damage following traumatic brain injury (TBI). The biological system is a newly developed rodent model of repetitive rotational head trauma. Methods include the rodent rTBI model, Cdk5-enriched phosphoproteomics, behavioral assays, electrophysiology, and pharmacological inhibition. The main contribution is identifying aberrant Cyclin-dependent kinase 5 (Cdk5) activity as a principal mediator of rTBI and showing that its pharmacological inhibition reduces the cognitive and pathological consequences of the injury.

paper_summaries.title: NPR1 in JazzSet with Pathogen Effectors.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper examines how pathogen effectors manipulate the NPR1 protein to establish disease in plants. The biological system is the Arabidopsis thaliana immune system and its interaction with plant pathogens. Methods and data types are not clearly specified in the abstract, as it is a review of molecular interactions. The main contribution is detailing the mechanisms by which pathogen effectors target NPR1, a master regulator of salicylic acid-mediated systemic acquired resistance, across different cellular compartments.

paper_summaries.title: Protein-Protein Interaction Network Analysis Using NetworkX.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper provides a methodological guide for extracting biological information from molecular interaction networks. The computational system involves cellular protein-protein interaction (PPI) networks. The primary method discussed is the use of the NetworkX Python package for network construction, visualization, and analysis. The main contribution is demonstrating how to computationally model and analyze PPI networks to understand functional regulations and predict interspecies interactions.

paper_summaries.title: Multiple membrane-cytoplasmic domain contacts in the cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator (CFTR) mediate regulation of channel gating.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the structural interfaces between nucleotide binding domains (NBD) and membrane-spanning domain (MSD) cytoplasmic loops in the CFTR channel. The biological system is the human cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator (CFTR) protein. Methods include cysteine cross-linking experiments, single-channel gating assays, and computational 3D structural modeling. The main contribution is verifying predicted NBD/CL interfaces and demonstrating that cross-linking domain-swapping contacts between opposite halves of the protein rapidly and reversibly arrests single-channel gating.

paper_summaries.title: A senescence restriction point acting on chromatin integrates oncogenic signals.
paper_summaries.summary: This study investigates the cellular commitment to senescence in response to oncogenic stress. The biological system includes human cells, benign pancreatic lesions, and pancreatic ductal adenocarcinomas. Methods include transcriptome analysis and chromatin accessibility assessments, though specific assay names are not clearly specified in the abstract. The main contribution is the discovery of a chromatin-linked senescence restriction point (SeRP) regulated by a transcription factor network (ETV4, RUNX1, OCT1, MAFB) that acts as a tumor suppressor mechanism lost in pancreatic cancer.

paper_summaries.title: Bridging the physical scales in evolutionary biology: from protein sequence space to fitness of organisms and populations.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper explores the integration of molecular protein properties with organismal and population fitness to understand evolutionary processes. The system encompasses evolutionary biological networks, protein sequence space, and population dynamics. Methods include a review of theory, computer simulations, and experimental data, though specific datasets are not clearly specified in the abstract. The main contribution is summarizing advances in linking the physico-chemical constraints of proteins, systems-level network buffering, and population-scale selection regimes into a unified evolutionary model.

paper_summaries.title: Genetics' Piece of the PI: Inferring the Origin of Complex Traits and Diseases from Proteome-Wide Protein-Protein Interaction Dynamics.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper examines how genetic polymorphisms contribute to quantitative traits and disease risk through intermediate molecular mechanisms. The biological system involves human biochemical networks and genetic variants. Methods focus on the application of protein-protein interaction (PPI) methodologies to capture the effects of genetic variation. The main contribution is proposing that the molecular etiology of complex traits can be better understood by characterizing the dynamics of biochemical networks using proteome-wide PPI methodologies.

paper_summaries.title: Neutral drift upon threshold-like selection promotes variation in antibiotic resistance phenotype.
paper_summaries.summary: This study investigates the conditions that promote the emergence and maintenance of heritable phenotypic variation in populations. The biological system is the VIM-2 β-lactamase antibiotic-resistance enzyme. Methods include long-term experimental evolution under static low-antibiotic selection and fitness modeling based on single amino acid variants. The main contribution is demonstrating that neutral drift under low antibiotic selection promotes significant standing phenotypic variation, allowing variants to confer resistance to much higher antibiotic concentrations due to a threshold-like fitness relationship.

cards.human_proposal_title: Elucidating emergent structures in cellular RNA-protein interaction networks

paper_summaries.title: The Rosetta All-Atom Energy Function for Macromolecular Modeling and Design.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the Rosetta Energy Function 2015 (REF15) for biomolecular modeling of soluble proteins, membrane proteins, and other macromolecules. The authors describe the mathematical models and physical concepts underlying REF15, parameterized from small-molecule and X-ray crystal structure data. The main contribution is explaining how to use Rosetta energies to identify and analyze the features of biomolecular models.

paper_summaries.title: Characterizing protein sequence determinants of nuclear condensates by high-throughput pooled imaging with CondenSeq.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the protein sequence determinants of nuclear condensates. The authors developed CondenSeq, a high-throughput pooled imaging and in situ sequencing approach, to measure the condensate-forming propensities of thousands of protein sequences. The study identifies context-independent sequence features and distinct properties that drive the formation of multiple classes of nuclear condensates.

paper_summaries.title: Macromolecular modeling and design in Rosetta: recent methods and frameworks.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper reviews recent methods and frameworks integrated into the Rosetta software suite for macromolecular modeling, docking, and design. The authors discuss improvements to the score function, user interfaces, and usability across over 80 methods developed over five years. The main contribution is providing an overview of Rosetta's expanded capabilities and interoperability for structural biology applications.

paper_summaries.title: Auto-DRRAFTER: Automated RNA Modeling Based on Cryo-EM Density.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies automated RNA modeling based on moderate-resolution cryogenic electron microscopy (cryo-EM) density. The authors provide a step-by-step protocol for the auto-DRRAFTER method, part of the Ribosolve pipeline, using a glycine riboswitch from Fusobacterium nucleatum as an example. The main contribution is detailing a successful implementation for automated RNA modeling to accelerate the understanding of RNA structure-function relationships.

paper_summaries.title: DAPTEV: Deep aptamer evolutionary modelling for COVID-19 drug design.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the generation and evolution of aptamer sequences for COVID-19 drug design. The authors developed DAPTEV, a deep aptamer evolutionary modeling approach, to target the COVID-19 spike protein with RNA/DNA oligonucleotides. The computational results demonstrate that DAPTEV produces structurally complex aptamers with strong binding affinities, offering an alternative to the conventional SELEX process.

paper_summaries.title: Dynamic mapping of proteome trafficking within and between living cells by TransitID.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the dynamic mapping of endogenous proteome trafficking within and between living cells. The authors developed TransitID, which uses tandem proximity labeling with TurboID and APEX followed by mass spectrometry, to track proteins across compartments like the cytosol, mitochondria, nucleus, and stress granules. The main contribution is mapping proteome trafficking networks, including the discovery that stress granules protect the transcription factor JUN from oxidative stress.

paper_summaries.title: Protein Phase Separation: A New Phase in Cell Biology.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the formation, regulation, and function of membraneless organelles via protein phase separation. Methods and data types are not clearly specified in abstract, though it mentions a combination of techniques from cell biology, biophysics, and bioinformatics. The main contribution is reviewing the molecular principles of protein phase separation and its implications for cellular organization and age-related disorders.

paper_summaries.title: A prion-like protein regulator of seed germination undergoes hydration-dependent phase separation.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies FLOE1, an uncharacterized prion-like protein in Arabidopsis thaliana that regulates seed germination. Methods and data types are not clearly specified in abstract, but involve molecular, organismal, and ecological studies. The main contribution is demonstrating that FLOE1 undergoes hydration-dependent phase separation to act as an environmental sensor, with natural variation in its condensation linked to adaptive germination strategies.

paper_summaries.title: Poly(A)-binding protein is an ataxin-2 chaperone that regulates biomolecular condensates.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the regulation of biomolecular condensates and stress granules, focusing on the neurodegenerative disease-associated protein ataxin-2. Methods and data types are not clearly specified in abstract. The main contribution is identifying a conserved 14-amino acid condensation switch in ataxin-2 and discovering that poly(A)-binding proteins act as unconventional RNA-dependent chaperones to control this regulatory switch.

paper_summaries.title: Current practices in the study of biomolecular condensates: a community comment.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper discusses current practices and physical concepts in the study of biomolecular condensates. The authors apply concepts from soft matter physics, such as aqueous two-phase systems and water-in-water emulsions, to describe these non-stoichiometric assemblies. The main contribution is outlining the tunable emergent properties of condensates, including interfacial tension and viscoelasticity, and distinguishing them from membrane-enclosed organelles.
