paper_summaries.title: Poly(A)-binding protein is an ataxin-2 chaperone that regulates biomolecular condensates.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the regulation of biomolecular condensates, specifically stress granules and the protein ataxin-2 in eukaryotic cells. Methods and data types are not clearly specified in abstract. The main contribution is the identification of a conserved 14-amino-acid condensation switch and the discovery that poly(A)-binding proteins act as RNA-dependent chaperones to regulate ataxin-2 condensation.

paper_summaries.title: Current practices in the study of biomolecular condensates: a community comment.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the current practices and physical principles underlying biomolecular condensates in cells. Methods and data types are not clearly specified in abstract. The authors outline how condensates function as non-stoichiometric assemblies driven by phase transitions, possessing tunable emergent properties like interfacial tension and viscoelasticity without requiring a surrounding membrane.

paper_summaries.title: Cellular Function of a Biomolecular Condensate Is Determined by Its Ultrastructure.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the relationship between atomic features, ultrastructure, and cellular function of the polar organizing protein Z (PopZ) condensate. The researchers utilized cryo-electron tomography, biochemistry, single-molecule techniques, and molecular dynamics simulations. The study establishes that PopZ's helical domain drives filamentation while the disordered domain inhibits it, with phase-dependent conformational changes exposing client binding sites in the dense phase.

paper_summaries.title: Emerging biophysical principles of macromolecular phase separation.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the emerging biophysical principles underlying macromolecular phase separation. Methods and data types are not clearly specified in abstract. The main contribution is a discussion of the physical rules governing how macromolecules separate into distinct phases.

paper_summaries.title: Mesoscale organization in bacteria.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the principles of mesoscale organization within bacterial cells. Methods and data types are not clearly specified in abstract. The work highlights how bacteria spatially and temporally organize their cellular components at the mesoscale.

paper_summaries.title: Physics-driven coarse-grained model for biomolecular phase separation with near-quantitative accuracy.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies sequence-dependent protein coarse-grained modeling for biomolecular phase separation in proteins like FUS, DDX4, and LAF-1. The researchers used atomistic simulations, bioinformatics data, experimental radii of gyration, and in-vitro phase diagrams to parameterize and benchmark the Mpipi model. The main contribution is the development of a multiscale model that accurately predicts protein critical temperatures and multiphase behavior by accounting for pi-pi and cation-pi interactions.

paper_summaries.title: Current practices in the study of biomolecular condensates: a community comment.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the physical principles and current practices for investigating cellular biomolecular condensates. Methods and data types are not clearly specified in abstract. The work describes condensates as non-stoichiometric assemblies governed by soft matter physics, highlighting their tunable emergent properties such as viscoelasticity and interfacial tension.

paper_summaries.title: Condensate Size Control by Net Charge.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies condensate size control mediated by net charge and electrostatic interactions in complex droplets. The authors employed molecular dynamics simulations and an equilibrium field theory. They demonstrated that long-ranged electrostatic repulsion can suppress droplet coarsening, leading to the equilibrium coexistence of equal-sized droplets due to ion expulsion and net charge acquisition.

paper_summaries.title: Exploring biomolecular energy landscapes.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies potential energy landscapes for predicting molecular properties and thermodynamics in proteins and nucleic acids. The researchers utilized geometry optimization procedures, local rigidification, and GPU implementations. The study highlights computational advances in structure prediction and kinetic analysis, demonstrating how mutations and structural transitions affect the multifunnel energy landscapes of biomolecules.

paper_summaries.title: Surface Electrostatics Govern the Emulsion Stability of Biomolecular Condensates.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the emulsion stability and fusion propensity of peptide-RNA and proteinaceous biomolecular condensates. The researchers combined single-condensate zeta potential measurements, optical microscopy, tweezer experiments, and multiscale molecular modeling. The main contribution is showing that higher condensate surface charge correlates with lower fusion propensity, highlighting passive stabilization mechanisms that protect condensates against coalescence.

paper_summaries.title: A Molecular Grammar Governing the Driving Forces for Phase Separation of Prion-like RNA Binding Proteins.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the sequence-encoded molecular grammar driving the phase separation of prion-like RNA binding proteins in the FUS family. The researchers used extensive mutagenesis and mathematical modeling. They identified that phase separation is governed by multivalent interactions among tyrosine and arginine residues, and developed a model showing saturation concentrations are inversely proportional to the product of these residues.

paper_summaries.title: The molecular basis for cellular function of intrinsically disordered protein regions.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the molecular basis for the cellular function of intrinsically disordered protein regions. Methods and data types are not clearly specified in abstract. The work discusses the biochemical and biophysical foundations linking the sequence of disordered regions to their conformational behavior and productive cellular functions, including intracellular information processing.

paper_summaries.title: Physical Principles Underlying the Complex Biology of Intracellular Phase Transitions.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the physical principles of intracellular phase transitions in biomolecular condensates composed of multivalent protein and RNA molecules. The authors applied a stickers-and-spacers framework adapted from the field of associative polymers. The main contribution is summarizing how the valence of stickers impacts driving forces for condensate formation and rheological properties, mapping the model to known drivers of biomolecular condensates.

paper_summaries.title: RNA-Induced Conformational Switching and Clustering of G3BP Drive Stress Granule Assembly by Condensation.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the mechanistic underpinnings of stress granule assembly via the G3BP protein. Methods and data types are not clearly specified in abstract. The study revealed that unfolded mRNAs outcompete G3BP auto-inhibitory interactions, causing a conformational transition that drives G3BP clustering and subsequent networked RNA/protein condensation.

paper_summaries.title: A prion-like protein regulator of seed germination undergoes hydration-dependent phase separation.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the hydration-dependent phase separation of FLOE1, a prion-like protein regulating seed germination in Arabidopsis thaliana. Methods and data types are not clearly specified in abstract. The researchers identified FLOE1 as an environmental sensor that phase separates upon hydration, suppressing seed germination under unfavorable environments and exhibiting natural variation linked to adaptive strategies.

cards.human_proposal_title: Multimodel single-cell frameworks for cell lines with extensive multi-omics data

paper_summaries.title: Leveraging AI to automate detection and quantification of extrachromosomal DNA to decode drug responses.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the rapid and reversible adaptation of cancer cells to epigenetic remodeling agents via extrachromosomal DNA (ecDNA). The biological system involves cancer cells subjected to drug treatments like JQ1. The researchers developed a post-processing pipeline using the Microscopy Image Analyzer (MIA) tool to analyze metaphase Fluorescence in situ Hybridization (FISH) images. The main contribution is an automated framework that effectively quantifies ecDNA dynamics under therapeutic pressure.
methods_or_data: Metaphase Fluorescence in situ Hybridization (FISH) images

paper_summaries.title: AI-Driven Variant Annotation for Precision Oncology in Breast Cancer.
paper_summaries.summary: This study investigates the functional impact of genomic variants of unknown significance in breast cancer. The system studied comprises breast cancer genomes analyzed for ESR1 and EZH2 activity. The authors utilized an AI/ML-driven framework integrating genomic, transcriptomic, structural, and drug response data from CCLE/DepMap and TCGA datasets. The work identifies structurally clustered mutations that share functional consequences with known oncogenic drivers, expanding the set of potentially actionable mutations.
methods_or_data: Genomic, transcriptomic, structural, and drug response data

paper_summaries.title: Kinase Plasticity in Response to Vandetanib Enhances Sensitivity to Tamoxifen in Estrogen Receptor Positive Breast Cancer.
paper_summaries.summary: This research examines mechanisms of endocrine therapy resistance in estrogen receptor (ER) positive breast cancer. The study utilizes ER+ breast cancer cell models and primary tumor short-term cultures. Methods include multiplexed kinase inhibitor beads-mass spectrometry (MIB/MS), CRISPR knockout models, and an operating room-to-laboratory assay. The study demonstrates that vandetanib treatment alters gene expression, upregulates HER2 activity, and enhances sensitivity to tamoxifen, with effects partially mediated by the RET receptor tyrosine kinase.

paper_summaries.title: Advances in the Management of Early-Stage Triple-Negative Breast Cancer.
paper_summaries.summary: This review paper explores the therapeutic landscape and management strategies for early-stage triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC). The biological focus is human TNBC and its inter- and intratumor heterogeneity. The study reviews clinical data regarding neoadjuvant therapy (NAT), immune checkpoint inhibitors, and targeted agents like PARP inhibitors. The paper summarizes current clinical practices, surgical de-escalation strategies, and molecular determinants of treatment response.

paper_summaries.title: The Need for Integrated Approaches in Metabolic Engineering.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper reviews state-of-the-art procedures and bottlenecks in heterologous small-molecule biosynthesis. The system of interest is heterologous host organisms used in metabolic engineering. The authors review strategies for manipulating the transcriptome, translatome, proteome, and reactome. The main contribution is the classification of optimization procedures and the emphasis on integrating multiple disciplines to create a framework for novel biosynthetic production routes.
methods_or_data: Systems biology classification (transcriptome, translatome, proteome, reactome)

paper_summaries.title: Genetic modifiers and ascertainment drive variable expressivity of complex disorders.
paper_summaries.summary: This study assesses how secondary genetic variants modify the clinical features of individuals with primary disease-associated variants. The biological system involves human cohorts, specifically 2,455 individuals with primary variants such as the 16p12.1 deletion, 16p11.2 deletion, and CHD8 variants. The researchers used network analysis and genomic sequencing data to evaluate rare and common variant classes. The study reveals that phenotypic associations differ by primary variant context and are influenced by synergistic interactions between primary and secondary variants.

paper_summaries.title: Genetic modifiers and ascertainment drive variable expressivity of complex disorders.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper investigates the role of secondary genetic variants in driving the variable expressivity of complex developmental disorders. The study analyzes genomic data from 2,252 individuals, including families with the 16p12.1 deletion and other primary variants. Methods include the analysis of short tandem repeats and single nucleotide variants (SNVs). The findings demonstrate that secondary variants have opposing effects on clinical features across different ascertainments and interact synergistically with primary variants.

paper_summaries.title: Protein misfolding involving entanglements providesa structural explanation for the origin of stretched-exponential refolding kinetics.
paper_summaries.summary: This research explores the structural origins of stretched-exponential protein refolding kinetics. The biological system studied is the protein phosphoglycerate kinase (PGK). The authors combined computational simulations with limited proteolysis (LiP) and cross-linking (XL) mass spectrometry (MS). The study concludes that misfolded states involving nonnative entanglements act as kinetic traps, creating a hierarchy of refolding timescales that explain the observed kinetics.

paper_summaries.title: Inferring protein fitness landscapes from laboratory evolution experiments.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper presents a statistical learning framework to model evolutionary processes and infer protein fitness landscapes. The system analyzed is the dihydrofolate reductase (DHFR) protein undergoing directed laboratory evolution. The researchers utilized sequence data sampled from evolving populations over multiple generations. The resulting model captures aspects of DHFR structure and function, identifies epistasis, and enables the in silico extrapolation of evolutionary trajectories.

paper_summaries.title: Inferring Protein Sequence-Function Relationships with Large-Scale Positive-Unlabeled Learning.
paper_summaries.summary: This study addresses the challenge of inferring protein sequence-function relationships from experimental data that lacks negative examples. The system involves various proteins analyzed through deep mutational scanning (DMS). The authors developed a positive-unlabeled (PU) machine learning framework to process large-scale DMS datasets. The method successfully estimates parameters that pinpoint key structural residues and was applied to design highly stabilized enzymes.

paper_summaries.title: The tumor suppressor kinase DAPK3 drives tumor-intrinsic immunity through the STING-IFN-β pathway.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper investigates mechanisms linking oncogenic mutations to immune escape in cancer. The biological system includes tumor cells, CD103+CD8α+ dendritic cells, and cytotoxic lymphocytes. The researchers utilized loss-of-function screening of tumor suppressor genes and comprehensive phospho-proteomics. The study identifies DAPK3 as an essential kinase that coordinates the post-translational modification of STING, thereby driving tumor-intrinsic innate immunity.

paper_summaries.title: TWEAK functions with TNF and IL-17 on keratinocytes and is a potential target for psoriasis therapy.
paper_summaries.summary: This study examines the synergistic role of inflammatory cytokines in driving dysregulated keratinocyte activity in psoriasis. The system involves mouse models with keratinocyte-specific Fn14 deletions and human keratinocytes. Methods include transcriptomic studies, imiquimod-induced skin inflammation models, and therapeutic antibody treatments. The research demonstrates that TWEAK acts alongside TNF and IL-17 to enhance inflammatory feedback, suggesting TWEAK blockade as a potential therapeutic alternative for psoriasis.

paper_summaries.title: Single-cell eQTL analysis of activated T cell subsets reveals activation and cell type-dependent effects of disease-risk variants.
paper_summaries.summary: This research explores the cell type-specific and activation-dependent effects of genetic variants on gene expression. The biological system comprises 19 distinct CD4+ T cell subsets isolated from 89 healthy human donors. The authors performed single-cell RNA sequencing on over 1 million cells and conducted single-cell expression quantitative trait loci (sc-eQTL) analysis. The study reveals that over 4000 genes are associated with common polymorphisms in a context-dependent manner, with significant sex-biased transcript enrichment in effector pathways.
methods_or_data: Single-cell expression quantitative trait loci (sc-eQTL) analysis
DICE (Database of Immune Cell Expression) datasets

paper_summaries.title: Intratumoral follicular regulatory T cells curtail anti-PD-1 treatment efficacy.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper investigates the cellular targets and modes of action of immune-checkpoint blockade therapies. The system studied includes tumor-infiltrating follicular regulatory T (TFR) cells in syngeneic mouse tumor models and human melanoma patient cohorts. The researchers used in vivo depletion assays and clinical survival outcome analyses. The findings show that TFR cells limit anti-PD-1 efficacy, and depleting them with anti-CTLA-4 prior to anti-PD-1 treatment improves tumor control and patient survival.

paper_summaries.title: Lineage-specific 3D genome organization is assembled at multiple scales by IKAROS.
paper_summaries.summary: This study examines how lineage-specific chromatin architecture is assembled to guide gene expression during development. The biological system includes B cell precursors and epithelial cells. The authors employed loss-of-function and gain-of-function approaches alongside genome editing techniques. The research demonstrates that IKAROS overrides CTCF-imposed boundaries to assemble lineage-specific regulatory units across megabase distances, preconfiguring the genome for lymphoid development.

paper_summaries.title: Machine learning in clinical care: Quo vadis?
paper_summaries.summary: This paper discusses the trajectory and integration of machine learning within clinical care. The system of interest is clinical healthcare environments. Not clearly specified in abstract. The publication provides commentary on the current state and applications of machine learning technologies in medical practice.

paper_summaries.title: Sequence-Based Prediction of RNA-Binding Residues in Proteins.
paper_summaries.summary: This chapter focuses on computational methods for identifying amino acids in RNA-binding proteins that directly contact RNA. The biological system is protein-RNA complexes. The authors review sequence-based computational tools, web servers, and databases containing protein-RNA complex information. The work provides step-by-step protocols for using web-based servers to reliably predict interfacial residues without requiring structural information.

paper_summaries.title: Predicting flexible length linear B-cell epitopes.
paper_summaries.summary: This study explores computational tools for predicting flexible length linear B-cell epitopes for applications in vaccine design and immunodiagnostics. The system studied is linear B-cell epitopes. The researchers evaluated machine learning approaches utilizing sequence kernels and feature vector mapping. The main contribution is the development of FBCPred, a novel method using a subsequence kernel that significantly outperforms other classifiers in epitope prediction.

paper_summaries.title: MetaScore: A Novel Machine-Learning-Based Approach to Improve Traditional Scoring Functions for Scoring Protein-Protein Docking Conformations.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper addresses the scoring problem in computational docking for determining the 3D structures of protein complexes. The system involves protein-protein interaction conformations. The authors developed MetaScore, a random forest classifier trained on protein-protein interfacial features such as physicochemical properties, energy terms, and evolutionary conservation. MetaScore, especially when used in an ensemble method, consistently outperforms traditional scoring functions in identifying near-native docked conformations.

paper_summaries.title: Connected in health: Place-to-place commuting networks and COVID-19 spillovers.
paper_summaries.summary: This research analyzes the impact of pre-pandemic commuter networks on population risk exposures to COVID-19. The system studied is US county-level populations and their commuting connections. The authors linked biweekly county COVID-19 data with Longitudinal Employer-Household Dynamics data using fixed-effects, spatial, and computational statistical approaches. The study shows that commuting network exposure predicted COVID-19 cases and deaths independently of geographic contiguity or pandemic-time mobility.

paper_summaries.title: Machine learning applications in genetics and genomics.
paper_summaries.summary: This review provides an overview of machine learning applications for analyzing large-scale genome sequencing datasets. The biological systems discussed include genomes, epigenomes, proteomes, and metabolomes. The paper covers supervised, semi-supervised, unsupervised, generative, and discriminative modeling approaches. The authors provide general guidelines for selecting and applying these machine learning methods to complex genetic and genomic data.

paper_summaries.title: A Genome-wide Framework for Mapping Gene Regulation via Cellular Genetic Screens.
paper_summaries.summary: This study presents a framework for mapping enhancer-gene regulatory interactions across the human genome. The biological system involves human cells subjected to random combinations of CRISPR/Cas9-mediated perturbations. The researchers used dCas9-KRAB to perturb 5,920 candidate enhancers and measured effects by profiling 254,974 single-cell transcriptomes. The framework successfully identified 664 cis enhancer-gene pairs, revealing their enrichment for specific transcription factors and 3D conformational proximity.

paper_summaries.title: A single-cell time-lapse of mouse prenatal development from gastrula to birth.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper establishes a global framework for exploring mammalian development by profiling transcriptional states. The biological system is the house mouse (Mus musculus), spanning embryonic day 8 to postnatal day 0. The authors applied optimized single-cell combinatorial indexing to profile 12.4 million nuclei from 83 embryos. The study constructs a rooted tree of cell-type relationships spanning prenatal development and nominates candidate transcription factor drivers for hundreds of cell types.

paper_summaries.title: Expanded encyclopaedias of DNA elements in the human and mouse genomes.
paper_summaries.summary: This publication summarizes phase III of the Encyclopedia of DNA Elements (ENCODE) Project, which expands the analysis of regulatory elements. The systems studied are the human and mouse genomes across various cells, tissues, and developmental stages. The project produced 5,992 new experimental datasets covering RNA transcription, chromatin structure, DNA methylation, and transcription factor occupancy. The authors developed a registry of over 1.2 million candidate cis-regulatory elements and a web-based server (SCREEN) to access this resource.
methods_or_data: RNA transcription and DNA methylation profiling

paper_summaries.title: MEME SUITE: tools for motif discovery and searching.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper introduces the MEME Suite web server, a unified portal for the discovery and analysis of sequence motifs. The biological features analyzed include DNA binding sites and protein interaction domains. The suite integrates multiple algorithms such as MEME, GLAM2, MAST, FIMO, GLAM2SCAN, TOMTOM, and GOMO. The platform allows users to discover gapped and ungapped motifs, scan sequence databases, and associate motifs with Gene Ontology terms for functional analysis.
methods_or_data: MEME and GLAM2 motif discovery algorithms
MAST, FIMO, and GLAM2SCAN scanning algorithms

cards.human_proposal_title: From image data and biophysical simulations to principles of mesoscale organization through integrated transfer learning

paper_summaries.title: Cilium structure, assembly, and disassembly regulated by the cytoskeleton.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper discusses the regulation of cilium structure, assembly, and disassembly by the cytoskeleton. The biological system is the cilium and its interactions with microtubule, actin, and septin networks. Methods and data types are not clearly specified in the abstract, as it is a review of recent advances. The main factual contribution is synthesizing how different cytoskeletal systems affect cilium function and organization.

paper_summaries.title: Primary cilium loss in mammalian cells occurs predominantly by whole-cilium shedding.
paper_summaries.summary: This study investigates the physical mechanisms of primary cilium loss in mammalian cells. The authors utilized live-cell imaging and modulated levels of katanin and intracellular calcium. The main factual contribution is the finding that mammalian ciliary loss predominantly occurs via rapid deciliation (whole-cilium shedding) rather than gradual resorption, and that excess katanin promotes this shedding independently of calcium.
methods_or_data: Modulation of katanin and intracellular calcium

paper_summaries.title: The short flagella 1 (SHF1) gene in
paper_summaries.summary: This paper examines flagellar length control in the model organism Chlamydomonas reinhardtii. The researchers combined experimental genetics with a computational model utilizing differential equations and stochastic modeling of cytoplasmic microtubule dynamics. The main factual contribution is identifying that the SHF1 gene encodes the TOG-domain protein Crescerin, which binds tubulin dimers in the cytoplasm and transports them into the flagellum to maintain length.

paper_summaries.title: Automated segmentation of soft X-ray tomography: native cellular structure with sub-micron resolution at high throughput for whole-cell quantitative imaging in yeast.
paper_summaries.summary: This research focuses on high-throughput quantitative imaging of cellular structures in Saccharomyces cerevisiae yeast strains. The authors developed a deep learning-based auto-segmentation pipeline for soft X-ray tomography (SXT) data. The main factual contribution is the quantitative 3D morphometric comparison of wild-type and mutant strains, demonstrating the utility of SXT for precise whole-cell and organelle curvature analysis.

paper_summaries.title: A scoping study of the whole-cell imaging literature as a foundation for the emerging field of cell anatomy.
paper_summaries.summary: This scoping study analyzes the trajectory and current state of the whole-cell volumetric imaging literature from 2004 to 2024. The authors systematically curated a corpus of 89 studies and 118 image datasets to evaluate bibliometrics, study design, and reporting practices. The main factual contribution is the establishment of a curated dataset of whole-cell imaging literature, highlighting trends toward small sample sizes and the need for standardized reporting practices.

paper_summaries.title: Centriole Biogenesis: Symmetry Breaking and Site Selection.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper discusses the mechanisms underlying site selection for centriole biogenesis during the cell cycle. The biological system is the centriole. Methods include the review of a computational study. The main factual contribution is highlighting how two interacting feedback mechanisms, autocatalytic activation and substrate depletion, can select a single site for centriole duplication.

paper_summaries.title: Simulated actin reorganization mediated by motor proteins.
paper_summaries.summary: This study investigates the reorganization of cortical actin networks mediated by myosin motor proteins. The authors developed stochastic agent-based models and data analysis measures to simulate actin-myosin interactions. The main factual contribution is identifying specific motor parameters, such as binding rate and step size, that generate distinct actin network configurations and demonstrating how different motor populations can act complementarily or antagonistically.

paper_summaries.title: Scalable Gromov-Wasserstein Based Comparison of Biological Time Series.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper presents a method for comparing biological time series data across different dimensions or unequally spaced points. The authors developed an optimal transport type distance based on a modified Gromov-Wasserstein distance optimization program. The main factual contribution is demonstrating that this scalable distance measure, along with Fused Gromov-Wasserstein barycenters, effectively retains characteristics of oscillatory time series trajectories during averaging.

paper_summaries.title: Efficient parameter generation for constrained models using MCMC.
paper_summaries.summary: This research addresses the challenge of finding parameter values that satisfy constraints in complex mathematical models. The authors proposed a Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) approach to efficiently explore a model's parameter space. The main factual contribution is the successful application of this MCMC methodology to analyze responses in a bistability-constrained model of protein phosphorylation.

paper_summaries.title: Unite to divide - how models and biological experimentation have come together to reveal mechanisms of cytokinesis.
paper_summaries.summary: This review examines the mechanisms of cytokinesis, specifically the contraction of the actomyosin cytoskeletal ring in animal and fungal cells. The biological system is the dividing cell. Methods discussed include agent-based modeling and continuum mechanics modeling. The main factual contribution is summarizing how mathematical modeling and biological experimentation have combined to explain the transformation of disordered cytoskeletal networks into coherent contractile rings.

cards.human_proposal_title: Transposable elements and the emergence of genomic innovation

paper_summaries.title: Protein-DNA binding in high-resolution.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper reviews experimental assays and computational analysis methods used for the ultra-high resolution genome-wide profiling of protein-DNA binding events. The biological system of interest includes transcription factors, nucleosomes, and RNA polymerases interacting with DNA. The study highlights methods and data types such as ChIP-exo, DNase-seq, and ATAC-seq. The main factual contribution is the synthesis of how these techniques enable the characterization of individual nucleotide interactions and the discussion of associated computational challenges.

paper_summaries.title: Domain-adaptive neural networks improve cross-species prediction of transcription factor binding.
paper_summaries.summary: This study investigates the viability of predicting cell type-specific transcription factor binding across related species using computational models. The biological system involves transcription factor binding sites and species-specific genomic repeats. The authors utilize neural networks, domain adaptation architectures, and ChIP-seq peak location datasets. The main contribution is demonstrating that an augmented network architecture correcting for domain shifts caused by species-specific repeats significantly improves cross-species predictive performance.

paper_summaries.title: PEGR: a flexible management platform for reproducible epigenomic and genomic research.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper describes the development of a web-based project management platform designed to track and quality control epigenomic and genomic experiments. The system targets high-throughput sequencing workflows composed of traditional biochemistry and informatics. The primary method is the Platform for Epi-Genomic Research (PEGR) and its integration with the Galaxy platform. The main contribution is providing a tool that supports rigor and reproducibility from experiment conception to publication-ready figures for both biochemists and bioinformaticians.

paper_summaries.title: Sequence and chromatin determinants of transcription factor binding and the establishment of cell type-specific binding patterns.
paper_summaries.summary: This review examines the sequence and chromatin determinants that establish cell type-specific transcription factor binding specificity. The biological system focuses on transcription factors, cooperative regulatory proteins, and dynamic chromatin landscapes. Computational approaches for characterizing, imputing, and predicting binding patterns are discussed, though specific datasets are not clearly specified in the abstract. The main contribution is proposing a model where transcription factor binding activities at individual sites operate along a two-dimensional continuum driven by either strongly favorable sequence features or chromatin context.

paper_summaries.title: Systematic integration of GATA transcription factors and epigenomes via IDEAS paints the regulatory landscape of hematopoietic cells.
paper_summaries.summary: This study investigates the epigenomic and transcriptional landscapes of hematopoietic cells to understand how GATA family transcription factors regulate target genes. The biological system spans mouse and human hematopoiesis, including hematopoietic stem cells, multilineage progenitor cells, and mature blood cells. The researchers utilized nuclease accessibility, CTCF occupancy, histone H3 modifications, and the Integrative and Discriminative Epigenome Annotation System (IDEAS). The main contribution is the creation of a comprehensive registry of candidate hematopoietic regulatory elements by segmenting epigenetic states across chromosomes and cell types.
methods_or_data: Integrative and Discriminative Epigenome Annotation System (IDEAS)

cards.human_proposal_title: Searching the crosslinking mass spectrometry universe for new protein-protein interactions

paper_summaries.title: Rapid discovery and evolution of orthogonal aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase-tRNA pairs.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the scalable discovery of orthogonal aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase-tRNA pairs for genetic code expansion. The authors use Escherichia coli as the biological system and develop a computational and experimental approach called tRNA Extension (tREX). The main factual contribution is the identification of 71 orthogonal tRNAs and 23 functional orthogonal pairs, including highly active amber suppressors.

paper_summaries.title: Optimized Loopable Translation as a Platform for the Synthesis of Repetitive Proteins.
paper_summaries.summary: This study investigates the expression of long repetitive proteins using a genetic construct that circularizes mRNA in vivo. The system utilizes a group I self-splicing intron from T4 bacteriophage and a fluorescence-based assay combined with directed evolution. The main contribution is the development of a loopable translation platform that achieves protein expression levels comparable to standard vectorial translation.

paper_summaries.title: Editorial: Biophysics of co-translational protein folding.
paper_summaries.summary: This editorial discusses the biophysics of co-translational protein folding. Not clearly specified in abstract regarding specific methods or data. The piece serves as an introduction to a collection of works on how proteins fold during synthesis.

paper_summaries.title: Electric Fields and Enzyme Catalysis.
paper_summaries.summary: This review examines the role of electrostatic interactions and electric fields in enzymatic catalysis. The authors discuss experiments utilizing the vibrational Stark effect to measure electric fields within enzyme active sites. The main contribution is the synthesis of these findings into a unified framework highlighting the importance of active site electric fields in accelerating chemical reactions.

paper_summaries.title: A Roadmap for Improving Reliability and Data Sharing in Crosslinking Mass Spectrometry.
paper_summaries.summary: This perspective addresses the reliability and data sharing challenges in crosslinking mass spectrometry for studying protein-protein interactions. The authors evaluate false discovery rate models and pipeline benchmarking methods. The main contribution is a proposed roadmap for community harmonization on error estimation, open data formats, and repository submissions to improve data dependability.

paper_summaries.title: A standardized framework for circulating blood proteomics.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper examines the challenges of integrating circulating blood proteome data across different studies and platforms. The authors analyze disparities arising from sample collection, pre-analytical handling, and mass spectrometry instrumentation. The main contribution is the proposal of a standardized framework utilizing high-quality, technology-agnostic reference samples to enable robust cross-study comparisons.

paper_summaries.title: The omics discovery REST interface.
paper_summaries.summary: This study presents the Omics Discovery Index (OmicsDI) REST interface for accessing and disseminating multi-omics datasets. The computational system integrates proteomics, genomics, metabolomics, and transcriptomics data with PubMed publications. The main contribution is the development of the API and accompanying R and Python libraries to facilitate programmatic access and impact estimation of biological datasets.

paper_summaries.title: Computational proteomics: Integrating mass spectral data into a biological context.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper discusses computational proteomics and the integration of mass spectral data into biological contexts. Not clearly specified in abstract regarding specific methods or data. The work focuses on contextualizing mass spectrometry results within broader biological frameworks.

paper_summaries.title: Universal Spectrum Identifier for mass spectra.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper introduces the Universal Spectrum Identifier (USI) as a standardized mechanism for tracing mass spectrometry proteomics findings back to their original spectra. The computational system encodes virtual paths to mass spectra deposited in public repositories. The main contribution is the implementation of USI across ProteomeXchange, providing access to over 1 billion identifications from more than 3 billion spectra.

paper_summaries.title: Proteomics Standards Initiative Extended FASTA Format.
paper_summaries.summary: This study details the Proteomics Standards Initiative Extended FASTA Format (PEFF) for high-throughput identification of proteins, sequence variants, and post-translational modifications. The computational format builds upon the standard FASTA format by adding a uniform mechanism for encoding extensive metadata. The main contribution is the formal specification and implementation of PEFF to facilitate proteogenomics and top-down proteomics applications.

paper_summaries.title: The effects of pathogenic and likely pathogenic variants for inherited hemostasis disorders in 140 214 UK Biobank participants.
paper_summaries.summary: This study investigates the effects of pathogenic variants associated with rare bleeding, thrombotic, and platelet disorders. The authors analyzed genetic and phenotypic data from 140,214 UK Biobank participants using genome-wide association studies and network-propagation analysis on a large interactome. The main contribution is the demonstration that common GWAS variants and polygenic scores can modify the penetrance and disease severity of rare variants in diagnostic-grade genes.

paper_summaries.title: π-HuB: the proteomic navigator of the human body.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper introduces the π-HuB project, an initiative to map the human body's proteome across various cell types and states. The project relies on multimodality proteomic datasets and computational sciences. The main contribution is the establishment of a collaborative framework to generate large-scale proteomic data for disease risk assessment, diagnosis, and drug target discovery.

paper_summaries.title: Network expansion of genetic associations defines a pleiotropy map of human cell biology.
paper_summaries.summary: This study explores the pleiotropy of human cell biology by expanding trait-associated genes from genome-wide association studies. The authors utilized network-based expansion across 1,002 human traits to identify shared genetic and biological processes. The main contribution is the identification of 73 pleiotropic gene modules linked to multiple traits, which can be used to map targets for drug repurposing.

paper_summaries.title: The Reactome Pathway Knowledgebase 2024.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper provides an update on the Reactome Pathway Knowledgebase, a curated resource of human biological processes. The computational system models biological processes as ordered networks of molecular transformations. The main contribution is the expanded annotation of the human proteome, disease-causing genetic variants, and small-molecule drugs, along with improved interoperability with resources like the Gene Ontology.

paper_summaries.title: A tissue-specific atlas of protein-protein associations enables prioritization of candidate disease genes.
paper_summaries.summary: This study maps tissue-specific protein-protein associations to prioritize candidate disease genes. The authors analyzed protein abundance data from 7,811 proteomic samples across 11 human tissues, validating findings with synaptosome cofractionation, pulldown data, and AlphaFold2 modeling. The main contribution is the creation of a tissue-specific atlas that reveals how cell-type-specific structures drive tissue differences and helps prioritize genes linked to brain disorders like schizophrenia.

cards.human_proposal_title: Intelligent metadata compilation to enhance the reusability and discoverability of mass spectrometry-based proteomics data

paper_summaries.title: The underappreciated diversity of bile acid modifications.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the repertoire of modifications to bile acids and related steroidal lipids driven by host and microbial metabolism. The researchers utilized a dataset of 1.2 billion publicly available tandem mass spectrometry (MS/MS) spectra, filtering for bile-acid-selective ion patterns to create a reusable MS/MS library. The main factual contribution is the identification of thousands of previously unrecognized modifications, including polyamine bile amidates in carnivores and humans, demonstrating the value of large-scale untargeted metabolomics data.

paper_summaries.title: Unified and Standardized Mass Spectrometry Data Processing in Python Using spectrum_utils.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the computational processing and visualization of mass spectrometry data in proteomics and metabolomics. The computational system is the Python package spectrum_utils, which handles spectrum preprocessing, machine learning applications, and plotting. The main factual contribution is the introduction of updates to the package that integrate community data standards, enhance processing capabilities, and unify data visualization.

paper_summaries.title: A universal language for finding mass spectrometry data patterns.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the extraction of patterns from untargeted mass spectrometry data to improve data utilization and reanalysis. The researchers developed a computational ecosystem centered around the Mass Spectrometry Query Language (MassQL). The main factual contribution is the creation of this expressive language, which allows users to directly query mass spectrometry data with defined patterns and enables the reanalysis of public untargeted metabolomics datasets.

paper_summaries.title: Discovery of metabolites prevails amid in-source fragmentation.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the discovery of metabolites in the context of in-source fragmentation during mass spectrometry. Methods, assays, models, datasets, or data types are not clearly specified in abstract. The main factual contribution is the assessment of how metabolite discovery prevails despite the presence of in-source fragmentation.

paper_summaries.title: From data to discovery: The essential role of computational tools in proteomics.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the essential role of computational tools in the field of proteomics. Methods, assays, models, datasets, or data types are not clearly specified in abstract. The main factual contribution is an overview of how computational methods facilitate the transition from raw proteomics data to scientific discovery.

paper_summaries.title: Lineage labeling with zebrafish hand2 Cre and CreERT2 recombinase CRISPR knock-ins.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the lineage tracing of hand2-expressing cells during zebrafish embryogenesis and larval organogenesis. The biological system involves zebrafish models utilizing GeneWeld CRISPR-Cas9 precision targeted integration, Cre/CreERT2 drivers, and loxP-based Switch reporters. The main factual contribution is the generation of endogenous hand2 Cre and CreERT2 drivers, which revealed that hand2 progenitors contribute to mesodermal, neural crest-derived, and venous blood vessel lineages.

paper_summaries.title: Ten simple rules for selecting a postdoctoral position.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the process of selecting a postdoctoral research position. Methods, assays, models, datasets, or data types are not clearly specified in abstract. The main factual contribution is a set of ten rules and guidelines for navigating postdoctoral career choices.

paper_summaries.title: Learning from the unknown: exploring the range of bacterial functionality.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies bacterial functional repertoires without relying on reference databases of functionally annotated genes or taxonomic markers. The computational approach employs a novel Fusion scheme and an alignment-free nucleic acid-based Siamese Neural Network model. The main factual contribution is demonstrating that this Fusion scheme outperforms marker genes in assigning taxonomic clades and successfully identifies shared functionality among highly divergent microbial homologs.
methods_or_data: Alignment-free nucleic acid-based Siamese Neural Network

paper_summaries.title: A primer on metagenomics.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the computational challenges and methodologies associated with metagenomics, focusing on uncultured microbial communities. The data types discussed include voluminous, noisy, and partial genomic sequences sampled directly from environmental habitats. The main factual contribution is a comprehensive review of the bioinformatics requirements for metagenomics, covering sequence assembly, gene calling, and function prediction.

paper_summaries.title: Tracing the ancestry of operons in bacteria.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the evolution of complexity in biological systems by tracing the ancestry of bacterial operons. The researchers developed a maximum parsimony algorithm and a software tool called ROAGUE (Reconstruction of Ancestral Gene blocks Using Events) to analyze complete bacterial genomes. The main factual contribution is the reconstruction of ancestral operon states, providing a vertical evolution model that illustrates how complex operons evolve from individual component genes.

cards.human_proposal_title: Emergent Order Parameters of Allostery: An AI Framework for Predicting and Engineering Protein Regulation

paper_summaries.title: The protein folding problem.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the fundamental puzzles of the protein folding problem, including the folding code, mechanism, and structure prediction. The system of interest includes foldable proteins and nonbiological polymers. Methods and data are not clearly specified in the abstract. The main factual contribution is the explanation that proteins fold quickly by solving large global optimization problems as a series of smaller local optimization problems, assembling the native structure from peptide fragments.

paper_summaries.title: Biotechnological and protein-engineering implications of ancestral protein resurrection.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the properties and applications of resurrected ancestral proteins derived from modern descendants. The biological system focuses on ancestral proteins and their modern counterparts. Methods include computational sequence reconstruction and experimental laboratory preparation. The main contribution is detailing how resurrected proteins display high stability, substrate promiscuity, and conformational flexibility, highlighting their potential for biotechnology and protein engineering.

paper_summaries.title: The Role of Conformational Dynamics and Allostery in Modulating Protein Evolution.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the fundamental principles behind protein evolution, focusing on dynamical properties that enable adaptation to environmental changes. The biological systems analyzed include modern proteins, resurrected ancestral proteins, and human exome mutations. Methods include the use of the Dynamic Flexibility Index and the Dynamic Coupling Index to quantify site-specific flexibility and dynamic coupling. The main contribution is providing evidence that the migration of functionally critical rigid hinges is a mechanism for rapid protein evolution, and that disease-associated mutations often alter flexibility at distal active sites.

paper_summaries.title: The protein folding problem: when will it be solved?
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the thermodynamic folding code, computational structure prediction algorithms, and the kinetic mechanisms of protein folding. The system involves proteins and non-biological foldable polymers. Methods include the analysis of Critical Assessment of Techniques for Structure Prediction (CASP) competition data. The main contribution is the finding that proteins avoid searching irrelevant conformations and fold quickly by making local independent decisions prior to non-local global decisions.
methods_or_data: Critical Assessment of Techniques for Structure Prediction (CASP) data

paper_summaries.title: Structure and dynamic regulation of Src-family kinases.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the structure and dynamic regulation of Src-family kinases, which are modular signaling proteins. The biological system comprises the SH3, SH2, and kinase domains of Src-family members. Methods include X-ray crystallography, biophysical assays, and computational studies. The main contribution is revealing the critical roles of the SH3 and SH2 domains in the down-regulation of the kinase domain and identifying conformationally distinct active states.

paper_summaries.title: Bile acids and the gut microbiota: metabolic interactions and impacts on disease.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the metabolic interactions between bile acids and the gut microbiota, and their subsequent impacts on disease. The biological system involves the human microbiome and bile acid signaling networks across distinct organs. Methods and data are not clearly specified in the abstract. The main contribution is highlighting how the gut microbiota manipulates the bile acid pool, which in turn affects infectious, metabolic, and neoplastic diseases.

paper_summaries.title: Interactions governing transcriptional activity of nuclear receptors.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the mechanisms governing the transcriptional activity of nuclear receptors. The biological system includes nuclear receptors, transcription factors, DNA, and coregulator proteins. Methods and data are not clearly specified in the abstract. The main contribution is summarizing how ligand-induced conformational changes influence inter- and intramolecular interactions to drive and modulate transcriptional responses.

paper_summaries.title: Illuminating ligand-induced dynamics in nuclear receptors through MD simulations.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies ligand-induced conformational changes and dynamics in nuclear receptors. The biological system is nuclear receptors and their associated ligands. Methods include molecular dynamics (MD) simulations and diverse methodologies for analyzing simulation data. The main contribution is providing a detailed examination of how MD simulations bridge the gap between static protein-ligand structures and the dynamical changes that govern nuclear receptor function.

paper_summaries.title: A phospholipid mimetic targeting LRH-1 ameliorates colitis.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the development of phospholipid mimetics as agonists for liver receptor homolog-1 (LRH-1) to treat colitis. The biological system includes the LRH-1 nuclear receptor and a murine T cell transfer model of colitis. Methods include crystal structures, binding affinity measurements, transcriptional activity assays, and in vivo murine models. The main contribution is demonstrating that appending phospholipid-mimicking groups to a synthetic LRH-1 agonist improves binding affinity, allosteric conformational changes, and ameliorates colonic histopathology in vivo.
methods_or_data: Murine T cell transfer model of colitis

paper_summaries.title: Ancestral sequence reconstruction for evolutionary characterization of proteins.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the evolutionary characterization of proteins. The biological system involves ancestral proteins. Methods include ancestral sequence reconstruction. The main contribution is the application of ancestral sequence reconstruction techniques to characterize the evolutionary history and properties of proteins.

paper_summaries.title: Metal-Binding Q-Proline Macrocycles.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the synthesis and structural properties of Q-proline-based, metal-binding macrocycles (QPMs). The chemical system consists of QPMs and metal cations. Methods include Fmoc-SPPS, peptoid synthesis, NMR, and racemic crystallization. The main contribution is demonstrating that metal-free QPMs are disordered but adopt ordered structures upon metal cation addition, with steric interactions driving the proline ring conformation.

paper_summaries.title: Open science discovery of potent noncovalent SARS-CoV-2 main protease inhibitors.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the discovery of noncovalent inhibitors targeting the SARS-CoV-2 main protease through an open-science campaign. The biological system is the SARS-CoV-2 main protease. Methods include crowdsourcing, machine learning, exascale molecular simulations, high-throughput structural biology, X-ray crystallography, and biochemical assays. The main contribution is the discovery of a noncovalent, nonpeptidic inhibitor scaffold and the generation of a massive, open-access dataset containing over 490 ligand-bound X-ray structures and 10,000 assay measurements.

paper_summaries.title: Assigning confidence to molecular property prediction.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies strategies for predicting molecular properties and quantifying the associated uncertainty. The computational system involves machine learning models, generative models, and binding affinity computations. Methods include data-driven property prediction and computational modeling of binding affinity. The main contribution is detailing how assessing uncertainty in property prediction models improves the reliability of high-throughput virtual screening and closed-loop drug design.

paper_summaries.title: Site-Specific Immuno-PET Tracer to Image PD-L1.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the development of a site-specific immuno-PET tracer for noninvasive imaging of the immune checkpoint protein PD-L1. The biological system includes the PD-L1 antigen and normal mouse models. Methods include amber suppression-mediated genetic incorporation of unnatural amino acids (UAA), PET imaging, in vitro binding assays, and ex vivo fluorescent staining. The main contribution is the creation of a homogeneous 64Cu-NOTA-αPD-L1 Fab conjugate that effectively visualizes and maps the biodistribution of PD-L1 in vivo.
methods_or_data: Amber suppression-mediated genetic incorporation of unnatural amino acids (UAA)

paper_summaries.title: Folding@home: Achievements from over 20 years of citizen science herald the exascale era.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the application of massively parallel distributed computing to biomolecular simulations of protein folding, receptor signaling, and ligand binding. The biological systems include various proteins, enzymes, receptors, and the SARS-CoV-2 virus. Methods include distributed computing via Folding@home, GPU-based computing, and exascale molecular simulations. The main contribution is summarizing over 20 years of technical and scientific advances enabled by Folding@home, including its critical role in understanding SARS-CoV-2 and aiding antiviral drug development.

cards.human_proposal_title: From Protein Knots to Pierced Lassos: Unraveling the Evolutionary Origin of Complex Topologies

paper_summaries.title: Molecular knots in biology and chemistry.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper reviews the prevalence and properties of molecular knots found in biological systems like DNA, RNA, and proteins, as well as synthetic molecules. The study examines the interplay between the structure, formation, and properties of these topologically intricate molecules. Methods include a review of experimental and computational studies. The main contribution is providing a comprehensive overview of molecular knots across different scientific disciplines.

paper_summaries.title: Hsp90: structure and function.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the structure and function of Hsp90, a highly abundant molecular chaperone involved in cellular homeostasis and stress response. The biological system focuses on the Hsp90 protein, its ATPase activity, cochaperones, and post-translational modifications. Methods include structural and mechanistic studies. The main contribution is detailing how Hsp90 acts on client proteins and is regulated by various cellular factors.

paper_summaries.title: Ubiquitin: a small protein folding paradigm.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper examines the 76-residue protein ubiquitin as a model system for understanding protein structure, stability, folding, and dynamics. The biological system is the ubiquitin protein folding energy landscape, including native, denatured, and partially structured states. Methods involve a comprehensive range of biophysical techniques. The main contribution is characterizing the experimental folding paradigm of ubiquitin.

paper_summaries.title: De novo design of knotted tandem repeat proteins.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper investigates the de novo design of proteins with complex topologies, specifically trefoil and pentafoil knots. The biological system involves designed tandem repeat proteins. Methods include tandem repeat protein design algorithms and X-ray crystallography. The main contribution is the successful design and structural confirmation of a trefoil knotted protein, alongside insights into the misfolding of a pentafoil design.

paper_summaries.title: How to fold intricately: using theory and experiments to unravel the properties of knotted proteins.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the thermodynamic, kinetic, and chaperone-aided effects involved in the folding pathways of knotted proteins. The biological system comprises knotted native state proteins. Methods include a combination of experimental and computational approaches. The main contribution is highlighting the complementarity of theory and experiments in unraveling the properties of intricately folded proteins.

paper_summaries.title: Theta-curves in proteins.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper characterizes the topology of connectivity circuits in natively folded protein structures. The computational system analyzes polypeptide chains featuring covalent, disulfide, and ionic bonds. Methods include cataloging topologies of theta-curves using coordinates from the Protein Data Bank. The main contribution is identifying and classifying the various topologies of theta-curves formed by bonds between consecutive and non-consecutive amino acids.

paper_summaries.title: Knotting pathways in proteins.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper investigates the folding processes and topological barriers of knotted and slipknotted proteins. The biological system involves small to large knotted proteins and their folding landscapes. Methods include numerical simulations and theoretical approaches. The main contribution is proposing that small knotted proteins fold via twisted loop formation and threading, while larger ones likely require chaperone support.

paper_summaries.title: Identifying knots in proteins.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper evaluates various algorithms used for the detection and identification of open knots in polypeptide chains. The computational system focuses on protein knot identification tools. Methods include comparing knot identification algorithms, specifically highlighting the uniform closure method and statistical approaches. The main contribution is demonstrating the advantages of statistical approaches based on uniform closure for characterizing protein knots.

paper_summaries.title: RiFNet: Automated rib fracture detection in postmortem computed tomography.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the automated detection of rib fractures in postmortem computed tomography (PMCT) scans. The computational system is a custom-made convolutional neural network named RiFNet. Methods include training and validating RiFNet, ResNet50 V2, and Inception V3 on a dataset of 585 PMCT images. The main contribution is developing RiFNet, which achieved a high F1 score and outperformed off-the-shelf transfer learning models for this specific medical imaging task.

paper_summaries.title: AlphaKnot: server to analyze entanglement in structures predicted by AlphaFold methods.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper presents AlphaKnot, a web server designed to measure entanglement in protein models solved by AlphaFold. The computational system evaluates protein structures from 21 proteomes. Methods involve analyzing AlphaFold predictions using pLDDT confidence values and generating matrix diagrams to identify knot cores. The main contribution is providing a public database and tool for researchers to classify protein entanglements as knots, unsure, or artifacts based on structural confidence.

paper_summaries.title: Theta-curves in proteins.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper characterizes the topology of connectivity circuits in natively folded protein structures. The computational system analyzes polypeptide chains featuring covalent, disulfide, and ionic bonds. Methods include cataloging topologies of theta-curves using coordinates from the Protein Data Bank. The main contribution is identifying and classifying the various topologies of theta-curves formed by bonds between consecutive and non-consecutive amino acids.

paper_summaries.title: Genus for biomolecules.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper introduces the 'Genus for biomolecules' database, which catalogs the topological structure and complexity of proteins and RNA chains. The computational system processes all RNA and protein structures deposited in the Protein Data Bank. Methods include generating genus trace plots and genus matrix diagrams. The main contribution is providing a self-updating database that links topological complexity with biological function for biomolecules.

paper_summaries.title: Proteins' Knotty Problems.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper explores the structural and functional roles of knots in proteins, particularly enzymes and DNA-binding proteins. The biological system includes knotted mitochondrial proteins and deeply embedded protein knots. Methods involve comprehensive topological analysis of the Protein Data Bank. The main contribution is discovering novel knotted structures and proposing a folding pathway where a loose knot forms at a terminus and slides into its native position.

paper_summaries.title: Knotting pathways in proteins.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper investigates the folding processes and topological barriers of knotted and slipknotted proteins. The biological system involves small to large knotted proteins and their folding landscapes. Methods include numerical simulations and theoretical approaches. The main contribution is proposing that small knotted proteins fold via twisted loop formation and threading, while larger ones likely require chaperone support.

paper_summaries.title: AlphaFold predicts novel human proteins with knots.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper investigates the presence of knotted proteins within the human proteome. The computational system analyzes over 20,000 human protein structures. Methods include AlphaFold and RoseTTaFold predictions, homolog search, clustering, quality assessment, and visual inspection. The main contribution is identifying 51 credible knotted proteins in the human proteome and discovering a potentially new complex knot type not previously reported in proteins.

paper_summaries.title: Uncovering the statistical physics of 3D chromosomal organization using data-driven modeling.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper reviews the three-dimensional organization of the genome and its role in mediating nuclear function. The biological system is the 3D chromosomal structure. Methods include data-driven modeling, maximum entropy approaches, polymer physics, Hi-C, DNA tracing, MiChroM, and MEGABASE models. The main contribution is demonstrating how combining polymer physics with maximum entropy approaches accurately models chromosomal ensembles consistent with experimental data.

paper_summaries.title: Structural reorganization and relaxation dynamics of axially stressed chromosomes.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper explores the relationship between the spatial organization of individual chromosomes and their emergent mechanical properties under stress. The biological system comprises mitotic and interphase chromosomes. Methods involve data-driven, coarse-grained polymer modeling and simulated axial stretching. The main contribution is revealing that chromosomes act as viscoelastic solids, with mitotic chromosomes being significantly stiffer due to lengthwise compaction driven by loop-extruding SMC complexes.

paper_summaries.title: Exploring chromosomal structural heterogeneity across multiple cell lines.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper investigates the structural heterogeneity and conformational changes of chromosomes across different human cell lines. The biological system is the 3D chromatin structure and genomic compartments. Methods include computer simulations, machine learning, polymer physics simulations, and microscopy data analysis. The main contribution is showing that epigenetic information can predict structural ensembles and that genomic compartment formation resembles hydrophobic collapse in protein folding.

paper_summaries.title: Residue coevolution and mutational landscape for OmpR and NarL response regulator subfamilies.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the residue coevolution and mutational landscape of DNA-binding response regulators (DBRRs) in bacterial two-component signal transduction systems. The biological system focuses on the OmpR and NarL protein subfamilies. Methods include coevolutionary analysis of bacterial amino acid sequences and coevolutionary landscape models. The main contribution is uncovering inter-domain residue interactions that stabilize inactive conformations, providing insights for engineering functional DBRR-based biosensors.

paper_summaries.title: Deciphering the structure of the condensin protein complex.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper predicts the atomic-scale structure of the prokaryotic condensin protein complex, which is essential for chromosome segregation. The biological system is the SMC-kleisin protein complex, specifically the homodimer of SMC and the ScpA subunit. Methods combine crystallographic data, coevolutionary information, and molecular-dynamics simulations. The main contribution is proposing a single-ring structure for the condensin complex and identifying configurational states involved in its functional opening and closing.

paper_summaries.title: Mechanisms of mechanical overload-induced skeletal muscle hypertrophy: current understanding and future directions.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the mechanisms underlying mechanical overload-induced skeletal muscle hypertrophy. The biological system is rodent and human skeletal muscle. Methods and data include a literature review of mTORC1 signaling, ribosome biogenesis, and satellite cell abundance. The main contribution is a comprehensive historical account and list of mechanisms associated with muscle hypertrophy, highlighting areas of disagreement.

paper_summaries.title: Guidelines for the use and interpretation of assays for monitoring autophagy (3rd edition).
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies guidelines for the use and interpretation of assays for monitoring autophagy. The biological or computational system is not clearly specified in abstract. Methods, assays, models, datasets, or data types are not clearly specified in abstract. The main factual contribution is providing updated guidelines for monitoring autophagy.

paper_summaries.title: Regulation of Ribosome Biogenesis During Skeletal Muscle Hypertrophy.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the regulation of ribosome biogenesis during skeletal muscle hypertrophy. The biological system is human and animal skeletal muscle. Methods include a review of existing literature on ribosomal RNA gene transcription. The main contribution is demonstrating that transcription of ribosomal RNA genes is necessary for increased ribosomal capacity and critical for muscle growth.

paper_summaries.title: Translational control: implications for skeletal muscle hypertrophy.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies translational control and its implications for skeletal muscle hypertrophy. The biological system is skeletal muscle subjected to high-resistance exercise. Methods include a review of protein synthesis rates and translational control mechanisms. The main contribution is detailing how increased protein synthesis after exercise contributes to protein mass accumulation per fiber.

paper_summaries.title: Molecular effects of exercise in patients with inflammatory rheumatic disease.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the molecular effects of exercise in patients with inflammatory rheumatic diseases such as rheumatoid arthritis and myositis. The biological system includes human skeletal muscle and chondrocytes. Methods and data involve in vitro mechanical loading, gene expression analysis, and muscle fiber cross-sectional area measurements. The main contribution is showing that exercise improves muscle performance, alters type I to type II fiber ratios, and reduces the expression of genes involved in inflammation and fibrosis.

paper_summaries.title: GPU-accelerated and pipelined methylation calling.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the acceleration of methylation calling in Nanopore sequencing data. The computational system involves CPU and GPU architectures. Methods include Hidden Markov Models (HMM) and the development of the Galaxy-methyl pipeline. The main contribution is parallelizing and optimizing the methylation score calculation on GPUs, achieving a 3x to 5x speedup compared to Nanopolish.

paper_summaries.title: Predicting Protein-Ligand Docking Structure with Graph Neural Network.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies protein-ligand docking structure prediction for drug discovery. The computational system utilizes Graph Neural Networks (GNN). Methods include the development of the MedusaGraph framework, which features pose-prediction and pose-selection models. The main contribution is generating docking poses directly via GNNs, achieving 10 to 100 times speedup over state-of-the-art approaches with slightly better accuracy.

paper_summaries.title: GPU-Accelerated Flexible Molecular Docking.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies GPU-accelerated flexible molecular docking for virtual screening. The computational system involves single-GPU and multi-GPU architectures. Methods include the MedusaDock platform and performance evaluations using a dataset of 3875 protein-ligand complexes. The main contribution is accelerating the coarse docking phase of MedusaDock, providing algorithmic and data structure optimizations for structure-based molecular docking.

paper_summaries.title: KegAlign: optimizing pairwise alignments with diagonal partitioning.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the optimization of pairwise genome alignments. The computational system is GPU-enabled nodes. Methods include the development of KegAlign using a diagonal partitioning parallelization strategy and comparisons with the lastZ tool. The main contribution is computing a human/mouse alignment in under 6 hours on a GPU while maintaining lastZ-level sensitivity for divergent genomes.

paper_summaries.title: KegAlign: Optimizing pairwise alignments with diagonal partitioning.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the optimization of pairwise alignments for divergent genomes to facilitate multiple genome alignment. The computational system utilizes an NVidia A100 GPU and 80 CPU cores. Methods include the KegAlign tool, diagonal partitioning, and benchmarking against lastZ. The main contribution is demonstrating a 150-fold speed improvement over lastZ for human/mouse alignments without the need for pre-partitioning input sequences.

paper_summaries.title: Cardiotoxicity concerns in total joint arthroplasty.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the cardiotoxic effects of elevated metal concentrations in patients who received total joint arthroplasty. The biological system is the human cardiovascular system. Methods include an editorial review of clinical study findings regarding cobalt and titanium levels. The main contribution is highlighting that elevated metal ions may affect cardiac structure and function, necessitating close clinical monitoring.

paper_summaries.title: Enhancing ulcerative colitis treatment with traditional Chinese medicine.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the efficacy of combining traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) with mesalazine for the adjuvant treatment of ulcerative colitis. The biological system is the human gastrointestinal system. Methods include a network meta-analysis evaluating clinical outcomes such as mucosal healing, quality of life, and recurrence rates. The main contribution is demonstrating that the combination therapy enhances mucosal healing and reduces adverse reactions compared to mesalazine monotherapy.

paper_summaries.title: Esophageal cancer: A global challenge requiring tailored strategies.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies screening and treatment strategies for esophageal cancer. The biological system is the human gastrointestinal system. Methods include an editorial synthesis of a review on esophageal cancer disparities and early detection methodologies. The main contribution is advocating for personalized screening and treatment approaches grounded in regional nuances and technological innovations.

paper_summaries.title: Mathematical model of atherosclerotic aneurysm.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the progression and interactions of atherosclerosis and abdominal aortic aneurysms. The biological system is the multi-layer structured arterial wall. Methods include mathematical modeling using a system of partial differential equations with free boundaries. The main contribution is identifying a 2D biomarker (cholesterol ratio and DDR1 level) for assessing aneurysm risk and evaluating the efficacy of anti-cholesterol and anti-DDR1 treatments.

paper_summaries.title: Advancing oral cancer care: Insights from Tongluo Jiedu prescription.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the use of traditional Chinese medicine as an adjunctive therapy in oral cancer management. The biological system is the human immune system. Methods include a clinical evaluation of 80 patients treated with the Tongluo Jiedu prescription, analyzing inflammatory stress markers and peripheral blood T-cell subsets. The main contribution is indicating that the prescription enhances immune function and reduces oxidative stress to aid patient recovery.
