paper_summaries.title: Intra-condensate demixing of TDP-43 inside stress granules generates pathological aggregates.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the triggers for the cytosolic aggregation of the nuclear protein TDP-43, a process associated with neurodegenerative diseases. The biological system focuses on TDP-43 within cellular stress granules. Using engineered TDP-43 variants, the study demonstrates that aggregation requires both up-concentration in stress granules and oxidative stress, which together induce intra-condensate demixing and subsequent pathological aggregation.

paper_summaries.title: Intra-condensate demixing of TDP-43 inside stress granules generates pathological aggregates.
paper_summaries.summary: This study investigates the mechanisms driving the cytosolic aggregation of TAR DNA-binding protein 43 (TDP-43) in the context of neurodegenerative diseases. The research utilizes iPS-motor neurons, a disease mouse model, patient samples, and engineered TDP-43 variants. The authors find that TDP-43 aggregation is driven by up-concentration within stress granules and oxidative stress, leading to intra-condensate demixing via local unfolding of the RRM1 domain and increased hydrophobic interactions.

paper_summaries.title: Expanding the molecular language of protein liquid-liquid phase separation.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper examines how specific polypeptide sequence features modulate protein liquid-liquid phase separation and the material properties of the resulting condensates. The study uses generated sequence variants of a repeat polypeptide with differing charge, glycine, aromatic, and arginine compositions. The findings reveal that diverse residue pairs work in tandem to drive phase separation, producing condensates that behave as viscous fluids with varying viscosities.

paper_summaries.title: ALS Mutations Disrupt Phase Separation Mediated by α-Helical Structure in the TDP-43 Low-Complexity C-Terminal Domain.
paper_summaries.summary: This research explores how ALS-associated missense mutations in the low-complexity C-terminal domain of TDP-43 affect its ability to form functional phase-separated ribonucleoprotein granules. The study employs nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy, molecular simulations, and microscopy to analyze in vitro granules. The authors demonstrate that a subregion of the CTD transiently folds into a helix to mediate phase separation, a process that is disrupted by ALS-associated mutations.

paper_summaries.title: Current practices in the study of biomolecular condensates: a community comment.
paper_summaries.summary: This community comment discusses the physical and chemical principles underlying biomolecular condensates in cellular compartmentalization. The biological system encompasses non-stoichiometric macromolecular assemblies that form via phase transitions. The paper outlines how these condensates possess tunable emergent properties such as interfacial tension and viscoelasticity, functioning without a surrounding membrane.

paper_summaries.title: Apolipoprotein E: Structural Insights and Links to Alzheimer Disease Pathogenesis.
paper_summaries.summary: This review examines the structural and molecular characteristics of Apolipoprotein E (ApoE) and its role as a lipid transporter and genetic risk factor for Alzheimer's disease. The biological system focuses on ApoE in the central nervous system and its interactions with receptors and amyloid-beta. The paper highlights historical progress in understanding ApoE physiology and its structural impact on neurodegeneration.

paper_summaries.title: Multiscale structure of chromatin condensates explains phase separation and material properties.
paper_summaries.summary: This study investigates the multiscale structure and interaction networks of molecules within phase-separated chromatin condensates. The researchers utilize cryo-electron tomography and molecular dynamics simulations to analyze mammalian nuclei and reconstituted condensates. The findings show that internucleosomal DNA linker length controls nucleosome arrangement and histone tail interactions, which in turn govern the thermodynamic stability and material properties of the condensates.

paper_summaries.title: Valence and patterning of aromatic residues determine the phase behavior of prion-like domains.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper explores the sequence features that determine the liquid-liquid phase separation behavior of prion-like domains (PLDs). The study employs nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy, small-angle X-ray scattering, and multiscale simulations. The authors demonstrate that the valence and uniform patterning of aromatic residues dictate the temperature-dependent compaction and phase behavior of PLDs, leading to the development of a predictive numerical model.

paper_summaries.title: Advancements in APOE and dementia research: Highlights from the 2023 AAIC Advancements: APOE conference.
paper_summaries.summary: This manuscript summarizes discussions from a conference regarding the multifaceted roles of apolipoprotein E (ApoE) isoforms in Alzheimer's disease pathogenesis. The biological context includes ApoE's effects on amyloid-beta, tau pathologies, lipid metabolism, and neuroinflammation. The paper outlines current progress in ApoE-targeted therapeutic strategies, disease models, and interventions modulating ApoE expression.

paper_summaries.title: Physical basis of the disorder-order transition.
paper_summaries.summary: This review discusses the application of polymer physics concepts to understand the conformational ensembles of intrinsically disordered proteins. The biological system involves proteins that lack stable conformations but perform essential biological functions. The paper details how residue-residue and residue-solvent interactions modulate conformational transitions within the disordered structural ensemble.

paper_summaries.title: Spermine modulation of Alzheimer's Tau and Parkinson's α-synuclein: implications for biomolecular condensation and neurodegeneration.
paper_summaries.summary: This study investigates how spermine modulates the biomolecular condensation of Alzheimer's Tau and Parkinson's α-synuclein in vitro and in vivo. The research utilizes time-resolved SAXS, NMR, and C. elegans models expressing these proteins. The findings reveal that spermine acts as a molecular glue to drive electrostatically mediated condensation, which promotes α-synuclein degradation via autophagy and ameliorates movement deficits in the animal models.

paper_summaries.title: The sequence-structure-function relationship of intrinsic ERα disorder.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper examines the sequence-structure-function relationship of the intrinsically disordered N-terminal transactivation domain of the estrogen receptor (ERα). The study integrates small-angle X-ray scattering, nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy, and functional mutational assays. The authors demonstrate that serine 118 phosphorylation causes an expansion of the disordered domain and disrupts specific hydrophobic clustering, which is crucial for ER transcriptional activity and target-gene expression.

paper_summaries.title: Phase separation to buffer growth-mediated dilution in synthetic circuits.
paper_summaries.summary: This research presents a strategy utilizing liquid-liquid phase separation to mitigate the destabilizing effects of growth-mediated dilution in synthetic gene circuits. The system involves fusing transcription factors to intrinsically disordered regions to form transcriptional condensates at target promoters. The study shows that these condensates buffer against rapid dilution, preserving bistable memory in self-activation circuits and improving production efficiency in a biosynthesis pathway.
methods_or_data: Fusion of transcription factors to intrinsically disordered regions

paper_summaries.title: F-53B triggers ovarian granulosa cell senescence and ovarian dysfunction by triggering mitochondrial dysfunction.
paper_summaries.summary: This study evaluates the toxicological effects of the persistent organic pollutant F-53B on female reproductive health. The biological systems used include cultured ovarian granulosa cells and in vivo mouse models. The authors find that F-53B induces cellular senescence via the cGAS-STING-IRF3 signaling axis and inhibits autophagy, leading to ovarian dysfunction characterized by reduced follicular reserve and altered hormone levels in mice.
methods_or_data: In vitro cell culture (COV434 and KGN cells)

paper_summaries.title: Biophysical and Integrative Characterization of Protein Intrinsic Disorder as a Prime Target for Drug Discovery.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper reviews the experimental and computational methods used to study the high conformational flexibility of intrinsically disordered proteins. The biological focus is on the sequence-structure-function relationships of these proteins and their potential as drug discovery targets. The authors highlight integrative biophysical strategies and summarize recent advances in developing small molecule inhibitors targeting the disordered N-terminal domains of transcription factors.

paper_summaries.title: Ghost admixture in eastern gorillas.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies archaic admixture and demographic history in great apes. The biological system comprises all four extant gorilla subspecies, including newly sequenced eastern gorillas. Methods include high-coverage whole-genome sequencing and approximate Bayesian computation with neural networks. The main contribution is the identification of up to 3% introgression from an archaic 'ghost' lineage into the common ancestor of eastern gorillas, which may have influenced bitter taste perception.

paper_summaries.title: Genomic Insights into Bear Hibernation.
paper_summaries.summary: This review studies the physiological and genomic adaptations associated with hibernation. The biological system focuses on bears as a model for mammalian hibernation. Methods and data include a review of transcriptomic and genomic studies across multiple tissues. The main contribution is synthesizing how differential activity in metabolic signaling pathways during hibernation could inform treatments for human metabolic disorders like type II diabetes.

paper_summaries.title: Integrating genomic and epidemiologic data to accelerate progress toward schistosomiasis elimination.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies strategies for the elimination of schistosomiasis as a public health problem. The biological system involves schistosome parasites and their human and non-human hosts. Methods include the integration of whole-genome sequencing with epidemiological and ecological data. The main contribution is outlining how genomic approaches can identify infection sources to tailor interventions and prevent transmission reemergence.

paper_summaries.title: A multi-tissue gene expression dataset for hibernating brown bears.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper presents a transcriptomic resource for understanding the complex physiological adaptations of hibernation. The biological system is the hibernating brown bear (Ursus arctos). The dataset includes gene expression data from 26 samples across 13 different tissues. The main contribution is the public release of this highly unique multi-tissue dataset to facilitate detailed investigations into hibernation physiology.

paper_summaries.title: Feeding during hibernation shifts gene expression toward active season levels in brown bears (
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the molecular mechanisms underlying the partial restoration of active season physiological phenotypes in hibernating bears fed glucose. The biological system includes adipose, liver, and muscle tissues from brown bears. Methods involve tissue-level gene expression analysis and inferences of upstream regulatory molecules. The main contribution is demonstrating that mid-hibernation feeding shifts gene expression toward active season levels, implicating regulators like PPARG in shifting metabolic phenotypes.

paper_summaries.title: Circadian gene transcription plays a role in cellular metabolism in hibernating brown bears, Ursus arctos.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the role of circadian rhythms in energy conservation and cellular metabolism during hibernation. The biological system consists of adipose-derived fibroblasts from brown bears cultured in vitro. Methods include time-series RNA sequencing, timed measurements of ATP production, and temperature manipulation. The main contribution is revealing that hibernation temperatures alter the timing and amplitude of mitochondrial and metabolic gene transcription, linking the circadian system to energy balance.

paper_summaries.title: Silicosis.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the occupational risk factors associated with the development of silicosis. The biological system is the human respiratory system exposed to environmental hazards. Methods and data are not clearly specified in the abstract. The main contribution is identifying that exposure to respirable crystalline silica from artificial stone significantly increases the risk of silicosis in workers.

paper_summaries.title: Irreversibility in bacterial regulatory networks.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper investigates the emergent property of irreversibility in bacterial regulatory networks, specifically focusing on transcriptional regulation. The biological system is the reconstructed regulatory network of Escherichia coli. Methods include network analysis of responses to transient single-gene perturbations and comparison with experimental data. The main contribution is predicting irreversibility in numerous cases and linking it to the proximity of perturbed genes to positive circuits, suggesting a connection to evolutionary adaptation.
methods_or_data: Reconstructed regulatory network of E. coli

paper_summaries.title: Opioid Overdose Prevention.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper addresses the topic of opioid overdose prevention. The biological system involves human populations at risk of opioid overdose. Methods and data are not clearly specified in the abstract. The main contribution is discussing strategies or factors related to preventing opioid overdoses.

paper_summaries.title: Accelerating Biological Insight for Understudied Genes.
paper_summaries.summary: This perspective paper examines the challenge of functionally annotating understudied protein-coding genes discovered through genome sequencing. The biological systems span multiple model organisms across all domains of life. Methods include proposing a transdisciplinary research model combining evolutionary biology, cell biology, genetics, and biochemistry. The main contribution is advocating for coordinated, multisystem approaches to overcome research biases and accelerate the functional annotation of understudied genes.

paper_summaries.title: Engineering Proteins Using Statistical Models of Coevolutionary Sequence Information.
paper_summaries.summary: This review explores the use of statistical models of protein sequences to understand coevolution and shared functional or biophysical constraints. The biological system is homologous protein sequences. Methods discussed include Potts models (direct coupling analysis) and statistical coupling analysis (SCA) applied to large multiple sequence alignments. The main contribution is detailing how these models detect local physical contacts and evolutionarily coupled networks, highlighting their utility for quantitative function prediction and de novo protein design.

paper_summaries.title: The need to implement FAIR principles in biomolecular simulations.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper discusses the management of molecular dynamics trajectories in the era of Big Data. The computational system involves biomolecular simulations. Methods and data are not clearly specified in the abstract, though it focuses on data management frameworks. The main contribution is advocating for the adoption of FAIR (findable, accessible, interoperable, and reusable) principles to promote open science and community reuse of simulation data.

paper_summaries.title: Autonomous Computing Materials.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper proposes a data-driven materials discovery framework for developing autonomous computing materials inspired by the human brain. The physical systems include excitonic, phononic, photonic, and dynamic structural nanoscale materials. Methods involve programming these materials for integrated sensing, computation, and data storage. The main contribution is conceptualizing materials that can operate in nonconventional environments and interface with biological sensors, overcoming the limitations of conventional computing materials.

paper_summaries.title: A Cuban Campesino in Chemistry's Academic Court.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper appears to be a biographical or perspective piece related to academic chemistry. The system is the academic chemistry community. Methods and data are not clearly specified in the abstract. The main contribution is sharing experiences or perspectives within the field of chemistry.

paper_summaries.title: Discipline-Based Diversity Research in Chemistry.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper introduces and formalizes the field of discipline-based diversity research (DBDR) within academic chemistry. The system studied is the demographic composition and professional culture of research-active chemistry departments. Methods include analyzing 20-year demographic data of women and under-represented persons of color (URPOC) professors and evaluating policies through biennial workshops. The main contribution is projecting future demographic trends and providing research-based recommendations for department chairs to advance inclusive excellence in chemistry.

paper_summaries.title: In vivo transformations of positively charged nanoparticles alter the formation and function of RuBisCO photosynthetic protein corona.
paper_summaries.summary: This study investigates how in vivo transformations of iron oxide (Fe3O4) nanoparticles affect the RuBisCO photosynthetic protein corona. The biological system is Arabidopsis thaliana plants and their chloroplasts. Methods include computational modeling, in vitro proteomic analyses, and carboxylation activity assays. The main contribution is demonstrating that positively charged nanoparticles preferentially bind to a RuBisCO small subunit, and that in vivo transformations of both positively and negatively charged nanoparticles significantly decrease RuBisCO carboxylation activity.

paper_summaries.title: Temperature-Sensitive Contact Modes Allosterically Gate TRPV3.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper investigates the molecular mechanisms of temperature sensing and allosteric gating in TRPV3 ion channels. The biological system is the TRPV3 channel protein. Methods include molecular simulations, multi-ensemble contact analysis, graph theory, and random forest machine learning models. The main contribution is identifying temperature-sensitive residue-residue interaction modes and demonstrating that specific contact states can predict the channel gate's state.

paper_summaries.title: Temperature sensitive contact modes allosterically gate TRPV3.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper investigates the molecular mechanisms of temperature sensing and allosteric gating in TRPV3 ion channels. The biological system is the TRPV3 channel protein. Methods include molecular simulations, multi-ensemble contact analysis, graph theory, and random forest machine learning models. The main contribution is identifying temperature-sensitive residue-residue interaction modes and demonstrating that specific contact states can predict the channel gate's state.

paper_summaries.title: Protein thermal sensing regulates physiological amyloid aggregation.
paper_summaries.summary: This study examines how eukaryotic cells form physiological, RNA-seeded subnuclear condensates (amyloid bodies) in response to environmental stressors like heat. The biological system involves eukaryotic cellular stress response pathways and constituent proteins of A-bodies. Methods involve manipulating structural pockets in proteins to observe aggregation targeting. The main contribution is proposing a model where a protein's thermal stability and temperature-sensitive structural regions act as intrinsic post-translational regulators for selective amyloid aggregation.

paper_summaries.title: Molecular drivers of RNA phase separation.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper explores the driving forces behind the sequence-, ion-, and temperature-dependent phase behaviors of RNA condensates. The biological system comprises RNA tetranucleotides, ssDNA counterparts, and chemically modified analogs. Methods include atomistic simulations to map equilibrium thermodynamic profiles and structural ensembles. The main contribution is revealing that magnesium ions promote lower critical solution temperature (LCST) behavior by inducing local disorder-order transitions, and that base chemistry and posttranslational modifications fine-tune RNA self-assembly.

paper_summaries.title: A Liquid State Perspective on Dynamics of Chromatin Compartments.
paper_summaries.summary: This review discusses the dynamic and stochastic nature of chromatin compartments within the eukaryotic cell nucleus. The biological system is nuclear chromatin, regulatory proteins, and RNA molecules forming membraneless liquid condensates. Methods discussed include equilibrium polymer simulations, hybrid non-equilibrium simulations, and mesoscopic field-theoretic models. The main contribution is synthesizing emerging theoretical paradigms and computational models that explain chromatin phase separation and liquid-like properties.

paper_summaries.title: Tribute to José N. Onuchic.
paper_summaries.summary: This publication is a tribute to a specific scientist. The system and methods are not applicable as it is a biographical or commemorative piece. The main contribution is honoring the work and legacy of José N. Onuchic.

paper_summaries.title: Characterizing the landscape of evolvability.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper investigates the landscape of functionally neutral variants to understand molecular evolvability. The biological system is a toxin-antitoxin protein complex. Methods involve an experimental framework to traverse a large space of genetic variants. The main contribution is providing insights into the evolvability and entrenchment of molecular interactions within protein complexes.

paper_summaries.title: CISD3/MiNT is required for complex I function, mitochondrial integrity, and skeletal muscle maintenance.
paper_summaries.summary: This study explores the role of the inner mitochondrial protein CISD3/MiNT in skeletal muscle maintenance and mitochondrial function. The biological system is mouse skeletal muscle cells and their mitochondria. Methods include generating CISD3-deficient mice, proteomic analysis, and coevolutionary and structural computational modeling. The main contribution is discovering that CISD3 deficiency causes muscle atrophy and that CISD3 interacts with NDUFV2 to donate [2Fe-2S] clusters, which is essential for complex I biogenesis.

paper_summaries.title: Biography of José N. Onuchic.
paper_summaries.summary: This publication provides a biography of a specific scientist. The system and methods are not applicable as it is a biographical piece. The main contribution is detailing the life and scientific career of José N. Onuchic.

paper_summaries.title: Information Theory in Molecular Evolution: From Models to Structures and Dynamics.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper reviews the historical and ongoing interconnections between information theory and evolutionary theory. The biological system encompasses molecular evolution models, protein structures, and dynamics. Methods and data are not clearly specified in the abstract, but the focus is on theoretical frameworks. The main contribution is synthesizing how information theory is applied to understand molecular evolution.

paper_summaries.title: Rhodopseudomonas palustris: A biotechnology chassis.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the utility of Rhodopseudomonas palustris as a chassis for biotechnical applications and industrial engineering. The biological system is the bacterium R. palustris. The study relies on a literature review of metabolic tradeoffs, biodegradation, and biofuel production data. The main contribution is a holistic summary of the organism's commercial applications, highlighting its metabolic versatility in converting diverse feedstocks into high-value products.

paper_summaries.title: Dissecting metabolic landscape of alveolar macrophage.
paper_summaries.summary: This study investigates the metabolic shifts that occur during the M1 and M2 activated phases of Alveolar Macrophages (AM). The biological system is mammalian alveolar macrophages. The researchers reconstructed context-specific Genome-Scale Metabolic (GSM) models and formulated a bilevel optimization framework called MetaShiftOptimizer. The main contribution is the identification of specific metabolic pathways, such as pyruvate and arachidonic acid metabolism, and key metabolites that drive M1/M2 polarization.

paper_summaries.title: Enhancing in silico strain design predictions through next generation metabolic modeling approaches.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper examines next-generation metabolic modeling approaches used for in silico strain design. The systems discussed are general biological metabolic networks. The methods evaluated include steady-state modeling, resource allocation, thermodynamic constraints, and kinetic modeling techniques. The main contribution is a critical analysis of how these frameworks can be applied to enhance the accuracy of strain design predictions and reduce the number of experimental design-build-test cycles.

paper_summaries.title: Dissecting the metabolic reprogramming of maize root under nitrogen-deficient stress conditions.
paper_summaries.summary: This research studies the metabolic reprogramming of maize roots in response to nitrogen-deficient stress conditions. The biological system is the root of Zea mays L. (maize). The study utilizes a genome-scale metabolic model (GSM) integrated with transcriptomics data from hydroponically grown maize, analyzed via flux-sum variability analysis. The main contribution is the prediction of metabolic shifts in central carbon and amino acid metabolism, alongside the identification of specific phosphatidylcholine and phosphatidylglycerol metabolites that support biomass production under nitrogen stress.

paper_summaries.title: Computational Approaches on Stoichiometric and Kinetic Modeling for Efficient Strain Design.
paper_summaries.summary: This book chapter reviews computational approaches for optimizing biological systems to overproduce target products. The biological systems include prokaryotes, eukaryotes, and microbial communities. The methods covered are stoichiometric (steady-state) modeling, kinetic modeling, and optimization-based strain design techniques. The main contribution is a detailed breakdown of three major frameworks used to generate testable genetic interventions for metabolic engineering.

paper_summaries.title: The genomic footprint of social stratification in admixing American populations.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies how sociocultural stratification and non-random mating shape genetic structure in admixed populations. The biological system is human populations in the Americas. The researchers used genomic ancestry data, mating models incorporating assortative mating and sex bias, and deep neural networks. The main contribution is demonstrating that socially constructed racial and gender hierarchies have significantly constrained admixture processes since European colonization.

paper_summaries.title: Interpreting generative adversarial networks to infer natural selection from genetic data.
paper_summaries.summary: This study develops a machine learning approach to detect natural selection and local evolutionary processes using fewer computationally intensive simulations. The system is human genomic data. The methods involve a generative adversarial network (GAN) comprising a fitted demographic model generator and a convolutional neural network discriminator, fine-tuned with custom non-neutral simulations. The main contribution is a powerful, interpretable tool that successfully identifies regions under positive selection in human populations by recognizing data that deviates from neutral demographic processes.

paper_summaries.title: INTERPRETING CONVOLUTIONAL NEURAL NETWORKS IN POPULATION GENETICS.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper investigates the interpretability of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) used for inferring evolutionary parameters like natural selection. The system is computational models of genetic data. The study employs SHAP values, dimensionality reduction, decision trees, and random forests to correlate learned network features with traditional summary statistics. The main contribution is revealing that CNNs implicitly compute statistics like pairwise heterozygosity and can efficiently approximate long-range linkage disequilibrium.

paper_summaries.title: Ancestral haplotype reconstruction in endogamous populations using identity-by-descent.
paper_summaries.summary: This research presents a novel algorithm for reconstructing the genomes of ancestral individuals to study allele frequency dynamics and disease inheritance. The biological system is an Old Order Amish pedigree from Pennsylvania. The method, named "thread", uses Identity-By-Descent (IBD) segments derived from genotype data across an extended pedigree. The main contribution is the successful reconstruction of an average of 224 ancestral individuals per chromosome, including the identification of a complex region harboring an Amish-specific copy number variation.

paper_summaries.title: INTERPRETING GENERATIVE ADVERSARIAL NETWORKS TO INFER NATURAL SELECTION FROM GENETIC DATA.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper introduces an efficient machine learning framework to detect natural selection without relying heavily on slow forward simulations. The system is human genomic data. The approach uses a Generative Adversarial Network (GAN) where a convolutional neural network discriminator distinguishes between real genomic regions and fake regions produced by a neutral demographic generator. The main contribution is demonstrating high power to detect selection in three human populations while improving model interpretability by clustering hidden units based on summary statistics.

paper_summaries.title: Greenlandic Inuit show genetic signatures of diet and climate adaptation.
paper_summaries.summary: This study investigates genetic adaptations to extreme cold and a specialized diet rich in omega-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs). The biological system is the indigenous Greenlandic Inuit population. The researchers utilized genome-wide scans for selection, single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) chip data, and membrane lipid analysis. The main contribution is the discovery of strong selection signals in fatty acid desaturase genes that modulate PUFA levels and are associated with anthropometric phenotypes like height and weight.

paper_summaries.title: Deep Learning in Population Genetics.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper reviews the application of deep learning algorithms for making population genetic inferences in complex evolutionary scenarios. The systems discussed include model organisms and simulated haplotypic data. The methods encompass discriminative and generative deep learning models with fully connected, convolutional, or recurrent layers. The main contribution is showcasing the feasibility of deep learning in demography reconstruction and designing a branched architecture to detect signals of recent balancing selection from temporal data.

paper_summaries.title: Archaic Adaptive Introgression in TBX15/WARS2.
paper_summaries.summary: This research examines a strong signal of positive selection in the Greenlandic Inuit genome to determine its evolutionary origins. The biological system includes human populations and the Denisovan genome. The study uses genome-wide selection scans, SNP chip data, DNA methylation data, and gene expression analysis. The main contribution is demonstrating that a deeply divergent haplotype in the WARS2 and TBX15 genes was likely introgressed from an archaic population and is associated with body-fat distribution and adipose tissue differentiation.

paper_summaries.title: The genomic footprint of social stratification in admixing American populations.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper explores how sociocultural stratification influences genetic structure and admixture beyond geographical factors. The biological system is admixed human populations in the Americas. The methodology involves deep neural networks trained on simulated admixture scenarios constrained by ancestry-related assortative mating and sex bias parameters. The main contribution is showing that socially constructed racial and gender hierarchies have historically constrained random mating and shaped admixture processes in these populations.

paper_summaries.title: ngsJulia: population genetic analysis of next-generation DNA sequencing data with Julia language.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper introduces a computational framework for estimating population genetic parameters from short-read sequencing data. The biological systems analyzed include pooled sequencing data and polyploid genomes. The researchers developed ngsJulia, a collection of templates and functions in the Julia programming language, including specific implementations like ngsPool and ngsPloidy. The main contribution is providing a flexible, efficient tool that accurately estimates genetic parameters even from low-coverage sequencing data.

paper_summaries.title: Genome-wide analysis in vivo of translation with nucleotide resolution using ribosome profiling.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies protein translation dynamics in budding yeast under rich and starvation conditions. The researchers utilized ribosome profiling, based on deep sequencing of ribosome-protected mRNA fragments, to monitor translation with subcodon resolution. The study defined translated protein sequences, identified extensive translational control, and observed widespread regulated initiation at non-AUG codons.

paper_summaries.title: Taurine from tumour niche drives glycolysis to promote leukaemogenesis.
paper_summaries.summary: This study investigates the molecular cues from the bone marrow stromal niche that engage leukaemia stem-enriched cells (LSCs) during oncogenic progression. Methods included temporal scRNA-seq, human LSC RNA-seq, in vivo CRISPR screens, and TAUT genetic loss-of-function mouse models. The authors identified the taurine-taurine transporter (TAUT) axis as a critical dependency in aggressive myeloid leukaemias, demonstrating that TAUT inhibition impairs progression and synergizes with venetoclax.

paper_summaries.title: In vivo protein turnover rates in varying oxygen tensions nominate MYBBP1A as a mediator of the hyperoxia response.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies in vivo protein turnover rates in mouse heart, lung, and brain tissues under varying inhaled oxygen tensions. Methods are not clearly specified in abstract. The research found that the lung proteome is highly responsive to oxygen changes, with extracellular matrix proteins stabilizing under hypoxia and hyperoxia, and nominated MYBBP1A as a hyperoxia transcriptional regulator.

paper_summaries.title: Methionine oxidation within the prion protein.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the misfolding and aggregation of the cellular prion protein (PrPC) into infectious aggregates. Methods are not clearly specified in abstract. The authors review evidence regarding the oxidation of methionine residues in PrPC by reactive oxygen species and its potential role in forming pathogenic prion aggregates.

paper_summaries.title: null
paper_summaries.summary: This study examines the role of O-GlcNAc Transferase (OGT) in the biogenesis and processing of lamin A. The researchers utilized a tail cleavage assay and mutation of OGT binding motifs and O-GlcNAc modification sites. The findings indicate that O-GlcNAcylation promotes lamin A processing, identifying a link between glucose metabolism and nuclear lamina biogenesis.

paper_summaries.title: Cannabinoid receptor 1 antagonist genistein attenuates marijuana-induced vascular inflammation.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the mechanisms by which marijuana increases the risk of cardiovascular disease and vascular inflammation. The researchers used UK Biobank analysis, in silico virtual screening, human iPSC-derived endothelial cells, and wire myograph in mice. The study identified the soybean isoflavone genistein as a cannabinoid receptor 1 (CB1) antagonist that attenuates Δ9-THC-induced endothelial dysfunction and atherosclerosis.

paper_summaries.title: Activation of PDGF pathway links LMNA mutation to dilated cardiomyopathy.
paper_summaries.summary: This study investigates the pathogenesis of LMNA-related dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) and its associated arrhythmias. The researchers modeled the disease in vitro using patient-specific induced pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes (iPSC-CMs) and electrophysiological studies. The findings show that the platelet-derived growth factor (PDGF) signaling pathway is activated in mutant cells, and its pharmacological or molecular inhibition ameliorates arrhythmic phenotypes.
methods_or_data: Patient-specific induced pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes (iPSC-CMs)

paper_summaries.title: Omics, Big Data, and Precision Medicine in Cardiovascular Sciences.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the application of omics, big data, and precision medicine within cardiovascular sciences. Methods are not clearly specified in abstract. The publication discusses the integration of large-scale data approaches to advance precision medicine in cardiovascular research.

paper_summaries.title: Cannabinoid receptor 1 antagonist genistein attenuates marijuana-induced vascular inflammation.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the attenuation of marijuana-induced vascular inflammation by the cannabinoid receptor 1 antagonist genistein. Methods are not clearly specified in abstract. The research highlights the role of genistein in mitigating vascular inflammation associated with marijuana use.

paper_summaries.title: Plasma proteomics mediate the association between degenerative joint diseases and dementia risk.
paper_summaries.summary: This study assesses the association between degenerative joint diseases (DJD) and dementia risk, alongside potential proteomic mediators. The researchers conducted a prospective cohort study using UK Biobank data, multivariable Cox regression, propensity score matching, and plasma proteomic profiling of 2,923 proteins. The analysis revealed that DJDs are independently associated with an increased risk of all-cause and vascular dementia, mediated by systemic proteomic alterations involving proteins like HAVCR1, GDF15, and COL6A3.

paper_summaries.title: A synopsis on aging-Theories, mechanisms and future prospects.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the biochemical processes and theoretical models underlying biological aging and senescence. Methods are not clearly specified in abstract. The authors summarize the multi-dimensional changes occurring during aging and emphasize the necessity of systems biology approaches to understand these mechanisms.

paper_summaries.title: Insights into the regulation of protein abundance from proteomic and transcriptomic analyses.
paper_summaries.summary: This study investigates the regulation of cellular protein abundances through post-transcriptional, translational, and degradation processes. The researchers surveyed mRNA and protein abundances using next-generation DNA sequencing and proteomics. The data demonstrate a substantial role for regulatory processes occurring after mRNA synthesis in controlling steady-state protein levels.

paper_summaries.title: Plasticity of the mammalian integrated stress response.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the plasticity of the mammalian integrated stress response (ISR), specifically focusing on mechanisms triggered by decreased eIF2B activity. Methods are not clearly specified in abstract. The authors describe a split ISR mechanism that activates the eIF4E-ATF4-PCK2 axis to maintain energy homeostasis through metabolic rewiring in the absence of eIF2α phosphorylation.

paper_summaries.title: Translon: a single term for translated regions.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the terminology used for translated regions in genomics and proteomics. Methods are not clearly specified in abstract. The authors propose the single term translon to describe these translated regions.

paper_summaries.title: Quantifying protein (dis)order.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the quantification of protein disorder and structural plasticity. Methods are not clearly specified in abstract. The research focuses on approaches to measure and quantify disordered regions within proteins.

paper_summaries.title: Fast, sensitive and accurate integration of single-cell data with Harmony.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the integration of diverse single-cell RNA-seq datasets across different technologies and conditions. The biological systems analyzed include peripheral blood mononuclear cells, pancreatic islet cells, and mouse embryogenesis datasets. The authors introduce Harmony, an algorithm that projects cells into a shared embedding to group them by cell type. The main contribution is demonstrating Harmony's superior performance and computational efficiency in integrating large-scale single-cell and spatial transcriptomics data.

paper_summaries.title: RNA velocity of single cells.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper investigates the estimation of RNA velocity to predict the future state of individual cells on a timescale of hours. The study analyzes single-cell RNA sequencing data from the neural crest lineage, developing mouse hippocampus, and human embryonic brain. The authors demonstrate that RNA velocity can be directly estimated by distinguishing between unspliced and spliced mRNAs. This approach provides a new method for analyzing developmental lineages and cellular dynamics in time-resolved phenomena.

paper_summaries.title: Interactions between cancer cells and immune cells drive transitions to mesenchymal-like states in glioblastoma.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper examines the interactions between glioblastoma cancer cells and the immune microenvironment that drive transitions to mesenchymal-like states. The study utilizes single-cell RNA sequencing of human tumors and model systems, alongside functional experiments. The authors show that macrophage-derived oncostatin M (OSM) interacts with receptors on glioblastoma cells to activate STAT3. The main contribution is highlighting how these cellular interactions alter the immune microenvironment and increase T cell cytotoxicity.
methods_or_data: in vitro and in vivo models

paper_summaries.title: Integrative single-cell analysis of transcriptional and epigenetic states in the human adult brain.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper maps the transcriptional and epigenetic states of cells in the human adult visual cortex, frontal cortex, and cerebellum. The researchers employ single-nucleus droplet-based sequencing (snDrop-seq) and single-cell transposome hypersensitive site sequencing (scTHS-seq) on over 60,000 single cells. By computationally integrating these multi-omics data, they identify regulatory elements and transcription factors underlying cell-type distinctions. The study successfully maps disease-associated risk variants to specific cellular populations in the human brain.

paper_summaries.title: Spatial transcriptome profiling by MERFISH reveals subcellular RNA compartmentalization and cell cycle-dependent gene expression.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the spatial distribution and subcellular compartmentalization of RNAs in individual cells. The authors use multiplexed error-robust fluorescence in situ hybridization (MERFISH) to simultaneously measure transcripts from approximately 10,000 genes. They develop an approach to determine RNA velocity in situ using the balance of nuclear versus cytoplasmic RNA counts. The main contribution is revealing cell cycle-dependent gene expression and spatial heterogeneity of transcriptionally distinct cells.
methods_or_data: multiplexed error-robust fluorescence in situ hybridization (MERFISH)

paper_summaries.title: The Evolution of Sub-diffraction Chemical Imaging from Nanoscale to AI.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the evolution of sub-diffraction chemical imaging from the nanoscale to artificial intelligence applications. The biological or computational system is not clearly specified in abstract. Methods, assays, models, datasets, or data types are not clearly specified in abstract. The main factual contribution is not clearly specified in abstract.

paper_summaries.title: Single-molecule microscopy for in-cell quantification of protein oligomeric stoichiometry.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper reviews methods for the in-cell quantification of protein oligomeric stoichiometry, which is vital for signaling and transcriptional regulation. The systems discussed involve target proteins within single cells. The authors evaluate fluorescence intensity-based, localization-based, and photophysical property-based single-molecule localization microscopy approaches. The main contribution is providing a systematic comparison of these methodologies to uncover structure-function relationships at the molecular level.

paper_summaries.title: Crossroads between membrane trafficking machinery and copper homeostasis in the nerve system.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper examines the interplay between membrane trafficking machinery and copper homeostasis in the nervous system. The biological systems discussed include neurons and models of neurodegenerative diseases such as Parkinson's disease and MEDNIK. The study reviews biophysical, cellular, and in vivo data regarding copper transporter distribution in different membrane compartments. The main contribution is summarizing how misregulated trafficking regulators synergize with copper dyshomeostasis in neurodegenerative pathogenesis.

paper_summaries.title: FDX1-dependent and independent mechanisms of elesclomol-mediated intracellular copper delivery.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper investigates the mechanisms of intracellular copper delivery mediated by the copper-ionophore elesclomol (ES). The study utilizes genetic, biochemical, and cell-biological approaches in copper-deficient cell models. The authors demonstrate that the mitochondrial matrix reductase FDX1 catalyzes the reduction of ES-Cu(II) to Cu(I) for the metalation of cytochrome c oxidase. The main contribution is uncovering both FDX1-dependent and independent modes of intracellular copper delivery by ES.

paper_summaries.title: Facilitated Unbinding via Multivalency-Enabled Ternary Complexes: New Paradigm for Protein-DNA Interactions.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the concentration-facilitated unbinding of DNA-bound proteins to understand gene regulation mechanisms. The biological systems reviewed include sequence-specific and non-specific DNA-binding proteins such as CueR, ZntR, RPA, and DNA polymerases in both in vitro and in vivo bacterial cells. The researchers analyze data from single-molecule magnetic-tweezers, fluorescence resonance energy transfer, and total internal reflection fluorescence microscopy. The main contribution is establishing that multivalent contacts enable the formation of ternary complexes, providing a general paradigm for regulating protein-DNA interactions.

paper_summaries.title: Single-Molecule Reaction-Diffusion.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies reaction-diffusion dynamics on a molecule-by-molecule basis using individual photon arrivals. The biological system analyzed includes the intrinsically disordered human linker histone H1.0 and its chaperone prothymosin α. The authors introduce Bayes-smRD, a Bayesian method that estimates kinetic parameters from continuous spatial positions and discrete state changes. The main contribution is enabling the extraction of single-molecule properties without surface confinement, using significantly less data than traditional fluorescence correlation spectroscopy.

paper_summaries.title: Single-molecule reaction-diffusion.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper investigates single-molecule reaction-diffusion by capturing individual photon arrivals to study fast molecular interactions. The system focuses on the intrinsically disordered human protein linker histone H1.0 and its chaperone prothymosin α forming ternary complexes. The researchers utilize the Bayes-smRD method to estimate kinetic parameters from thousands of photon arrivals. The main contribution is demonstrating that this approach avoids bulk averaging and surface confinement while dramatically reducing sample photodamage.

paper_summaries.title: Hydrodynamic Hunters.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper explores the hunting dynamics of the bacterial predator Bdellovibrio bacteriovorus targeting Escherichia coli. The study employs experimental controls and hydrodynamic calculations to model predator-prey interactions. The authors find that self-generated hydrodynamic flow fields force the predator onto surfaces and into orbital motion around defects. The main contribution is revealing that hydrodynamics, rather than chemical cues, colocalizes predator and prey by reducing the search space from three dimensions to two or one.

paper_summaries.title: Single-Photon Single-Particle Tracking.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of tracking fast-diffusing biological particles using microsecond-scale exposures and binary output. The systems validated include programmed fluorescent bead trajectories and biological molecules like aerolysin and ganglioside. The authors introduce single-photon single-particle tracking (SP2T), a framework that estimates particle numbers and trajectories directly from 1-bit image stacks using single-photon avalanche diode (SPAD) arrays. The main contribution is providing a robust, data-efficient solution for unbiased particle tracking that achieves substantial computational speedups over CPU-based methods.

paper_summaries.title: Fluorescence Microscopy: a statistics-optics perspective.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper reviews the statistical and optical principles underlying fluorescence microscopy. The study focuses on the probabilistic modeling tools required to interpret images collected at scales near or below the wavelength of light. The authors discuss the optics responsible for generating fluorescent images and the specific properties of fluorophores. The main contribution is providing a comprehensive perspective on how the stochastic nature of light and measurement imposes fundamental features on microscopy images.

paper_summaries.title: Cooperative DNA looping by PRC2 complexes.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the structural conformations and DNA interactions of the Polycomb repressive complex 2 (PRC2). Using molecular dynamics simulations and single-molecule force spectroscopy, the authors characterize how the EZH2 and SUZ12 subunits interact with and bend DNA. The main factual contribution is the finding that multiple PRC2 complexes bind DNA cooperatively to form hairpin-like loops, a process regulated by accessory proteins like AEBP2.
methods_or_data: Atomistic and coarse-grained molecular dynamics simulations

paper_summaries.title: Connected Chromatin Amplifies Acetylation-Modulated Nucleosome Interactions.
paper_summaries.summary: This study investigates how H4K16 acetylation (H4K16ac) influences higher-order chromatin organization and nucleosome interactions. The authors utilized a residue-resolution coarse-grained chromatin model and enhanced sampling techniques to simulate charge-neutralization effects. They found that H4K16ac stabilizes single nucleosomes but weakens internucleosome interactions, leading to significant chromatin destacking and decompaction when nucleosomes are connected by linker DNA.

paper_summaries.title: Ligand-induced transmembrane conformational coupling in monomeric EGFR.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper examines ligand-induced transmembrane signaling within monomeric, full-length epidermal growth factor receptors (EGFR). By combining membrane nanodiscs, single-molecule FRET, and molecular dynamics simulations, the researchers observed intracellular conformational changes triggered by extracellular ligand binding. The study establishes the existence of intramolecular transmembrane conformational coupling mediated by electrostatic interactions, which can be inhibited by targeted therapeutics.

paper_summaries.title: PANoptosis-related genes in the prognosis and immune landscape of hepatocellular carcinoma.
paper_summaries.summary: This research explores the prognostic and immunological role of PANoptosis-related genes (PRGs) in hepatocellular carcinoma. The authors used consensus clustering and LASSO regression on TCGA-LIHC and ICGC datasets to establish a six-gene PRG signature. The main contribution is the development of a predictive nomogram combining this signature with clinicopathological features, revealing that low-risk groups exhibit distinct immune infiltration profiles and better prognoses.

paper_summaries.title: Chromatin fiber breaks into clutches under tension and crowding.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper characterizes the structural organization and unfolding of chromatin fibers under tension and crowding conditions. Using a residue-level coarse-grained model, the authors computed force-extension curves that match single-molecule experimental data. They demonstrated that a dodeca-nucleosome in a zigzag conformation breaks into nucleosome clutches and smaller oligomers under tension, suggesting a mechanism for the irregularity of in vivo chromatin configurations.

paper_summaries.title: Single-cell multiregion epigenomic rewiring in Alzheimer's disease progression and cognitive resilience.
paper_summaries.summary: This study maps the epigenomic and transcriptomic landscape of Alzheimer's disease (AD) progression using 3.5 million cells from 384 postmortem brain samples. The authors generated single-cell profiles to identify over 1 million candidate cis-regulatory elements and define large-scale epigenomic compartments. The main contribution is the discovery of widespread, brain-region-specific, and cell-type-specific epigenomic erosion that correlates with AD pathology, glial state transitions, and cognitive resilience.

paper_summaries.title: Histone acetyltransferase Kat2a regulates ferroptosis via enhancing Tfrc and Hmox1 expression in diabetic cardiomyopathy.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper investigates the role of the histone acetyltransferase Kat2a and its N6-methyladenosine (m6A) modification in diabetic cardiomyopathy. The authors found that Kat2a expression is upregulated in DCM due to reduced m6A methylation mediated by Alkbh5 and Ythdf2. The study demonstrates that Kat2a promotes cardiomyocyte ferroptosis by increasing Tfrc and Hmox1 expression via enhanced H3K27ac and H3K9ac enrichment at their promoters.
methods_or_data: In vitro and in vivo models

paper_summaries.title: Longitudinal assessment of coronary plaque regression related to sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitor using coronary computed tomography angiography.
paper_summaries.summary: This longitudinal cohort study evaluates the effect of Sodium-Glucose Cotransporter-2 Inhibitors (SGLT2i) on coronary atherosclerosis progression in patients with type 2 diabetes. Using serial coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) and propensity score matching, the authors measured plaque volume and percent atheroma volume. They found that SGLT2i therapy is significantly associated with the regression of overall and non-calcified coronary plaque volumes.

paper_summaries.title: Association of pericoronary inflammation with atherosclerotic plaque progression in diabetic patients with improved modifiable cardiovascular risk factors: a longitudinal CCTA cohort study.
paper_summaries.summary: This research assesses the relationship between pericoronary adipose tissue (PCAT) attenuation and atherosclerotic plaque progression in diabetic patients with improved modifiable cardiovascular risk factors. The authors analyzed serial CCTA scans to measure changes in percent atheroma volume and PCAT attenuation over time. The main finding is that increased pericoronary inflammation, indicated by elevated PCAT attenuation, is independently associated with the progression of overall and non-calcified atherosclerotic plaques.

paper_summaries.title: Single-cell RNA sequencing data imputation using bi-level feature propagation.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper introduces single-cell bilevel feature propagation (scBFP), a computational method designed to impute missing values and denoise single-cell RNA sequencing data. The method uses a two-step graph-based approach that leverages both gene-gene and cell-cell relationships without altering non-zero values affected by dropout. The main contribution is demonstrating that scBFP effectively mitigates technical noise and sparsity, improving downstream analyses of cellular heterogeneity.

paper_summaries.title: Fasting-mimicking diet-enriched Bifidobacterium pseudolongum promotes antitumour immunity in colorectal cancer.
paper_summaries.summary: This study investigates how a fasting-mimicking diet (FMD) modulates the gut microbiota to protect against colorectal cancer. Using metagenomic and metabolomic profiling alongside single-cell RNA sequencing, the authors identified the enrichment of Bifidobacterium pseudolongum and its metabolite L-arginine in FMD-treated subjects. The main finding is that B. pseudolongum-derived L-arginine promotes the differentiation of CD8+ T-cells into tissue-resident memory cells, enhancing anti-tumor immunity and anti-CTLA-4 efficacy.

paper_summaries.title: Deconstructing the intercellular interactome in vascular dementia with focal ischemia for therapeutic applications.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper maps the dysregulated intercellular signaling pathways in vascular dementia using a focal ischemia mouse model and human single-nucleus RNA sequencing data. The authors integrated transcriptomes across species using a custom ligand-receptor database to identify conserved disrupted pathways. They demonstrated that modulating the Serpine2-Lrp1 and CD39-A3AR signaling systems can promote oligodendrocyte progenitor cell differentiation and restore tissue integrity in the VaD model.

paper_summaries.title: Lactylation in Tumor Immune Escape and Immunotherapy: Multifaceted Functions and Therapeutic Strategies.
paper_summaries.summary: This review article examines the role of lysine lactylation, a posttranslational modification driven by lactate, in tumor immune microenvironment remodeling and cancer progression. The authors synthesize existing research on how the Warburg effect and elevated lactate concentrations influence tumor metastasis and immune escape. The paper outlines the molecular mechanisms of lactylation and discusses emerging therapeutic strategies, including small-molecule inhibitors and nanoparticle-based approaches.

paper_summaries.title: Proteomic subtypes enrich current acute myeloid leukemia nomenclature and reflect intrinsic pathogenesis alongside aging.
paper_summaries.summary: This study establishes a proteomics-based classification system for acute myeloid leukemia to better understand its pathogenesis and aging-related features. By integrating multiomics data from 374 newly diagnosed patients using similarity network fusion clustering, the authors identified 8 distinct proteomic subtypes. The main contribution is the development of a hematopoietic aging score based on megakaryocyte and immune-related protein networks, which correlates with specific mutations and patient prognosis.

paper_summaries.title: Targeting Msx2 as a brake in the fusion fate of osteoclasts and an anabolic therapy in pre-clinical models of osteoporosis.
paper_summaries.summary: This research explores the role of the homeobox gene MSX2 in adult bone resorption and osteoclast fusion. Using myeloid-specific Msx2 deficient mice, the authors found that loss of Msx2 halts osteoclast fusion, leading to an accumulation of pre-osteoclasts that secrete PDGF-BB to promote angiogenesis-mediated bone formation. The study identifies MSX2 as a protector of the transcription factor PU.1 from degradation and demonstrates that the natural compound morusinol can disrupt this interaction to attenuate bone loss.

paper_summaries.title: antiSMASH 8.0: extended gene cluster detection capabilities and analyses of chemistry, enzymology, and regulation.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper presents version 8 of antiSMASH, a computational tool for detecting and characterizing biosynthetic gene clusters in microbial genomes. The authors updated the software to increase the number of detectable cluster types from 81 to 101. The main contribution is the enhancement of predictive capabilities for natural product genome mining, including improved analysis support for terpenoids, tailoring enzymes, and modular enzymes like polyketide synthases.

paper_summaries.title: The oncogene SLC35F2 is a high-specificity transporter for the micronutrients queuine and queuosine.
paper_summaries.summary: This study identifies the oncogene SLC35F2 as the specific cellular transporter for the bacterial-derived micronutrients queuine and queuosine. Using bioinformatic searches, genetic disruption in HeLa cells, and uptake assays, the authors characterized the binding affinities and localization of SLC35F2 to the cell membrane and Golgi apparatus. The main factual contribution is establishing SLC35F2 as a highly selective, high-affinity transporter essential for the cellular acquisition of these micronutrients.

paper_summaries.title: The ubiquitous pyridoxal 5'-phosphate-binding protein is also an RNA-binding protein.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper investigates the cellular function of the ubiquitous pyridoxal 5'-phosphate binding protein (PLP-BP), known as YggS in E. coli. Through co-purification and RNA-seq analysis, the authors discovered that YggS binds specifically to SsrA and RnpB RNAs, which are involved in trans-translation and tRNA maturation. The study demonstrates that this evolutionarily conserved RNA-binding activity is modulated by PLP and relies on an invariant lysine residue, suggesting a novel regulatory role for PLP-BP.

paper_summaries.title: Functional redundancy in tRNA dihydrouridylation.
paper_summaries.summary: This research explores the mechanisms of dihydrouridine (D) biosynthesis in the transfer RNA of Bacillus subtilis. Using genetic and epitranscriptomic mapping techniques, the authors identified two FMN-dependent flavoproteins, DusB1 and DusB2, responsible for introducing D residues into tRNAs. The main finding is a functional redundancy between these enzymes, with DusB2 showing higher efficiency, which is critical for bacterial growth and adaptation at suboptimal temperatures.

paper_summaries.title: Are Bacterial Processes Dependent on Global Ribosome Pausing Affected by tRNA Modification Defects?
paper_summaries.summary: This paper hypothesizes that defects in tRNA modifications broadly disrupt bacterial processes sensitive to translation speed, such as global ribosome pausing. By integrating transcriptomic, proteomic, and phenotypic data from E. coli and V. cholerae, the authors analyzed the translation of regulatory proteins linked to motility, iron homeostasis, and attenuation mechanisms. The main contribution is providing a foundational framework showing how single or multiple tRNA modification absences impact translation speed-dependent cellular functions.

paper_summaries.title: Proteolethargy is a pathogenic mechanism in chronic disease.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies reduced protein mobility, termed proteolethargy, in chronic diseases like diabetes and inflammation. The biological system comprises cellular proteins affected by pathogenic signaling. Methods and data types are not clearly specified in the abstract. The main contribution is proposing that proteolethargy, linked to cysteine residues and reactive oxygen species, is a widespread pathogenic mechanism in chronic diseases.

paper_summaries.title: Rewiring endogenous genes in CAR T cells for tumour-restricted payload delivery.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the targeted delivery of cytokines in CAR T cell therapy for solid tumors. The biological systems include CAR T cells, syngeneic and xenogeneic mouse models, and human patient cells. Methods include CRISPR knock-in and screening of endogenous promoters like NR4A2 and RGS16. The main contribution is developing a strategy to rewire endogenous genes for tumor-restricted cytokine delivery, enhancing antitumor efficacy and safety.

paper_summaries.title: The mutagenic forces shaping the genomes of lung cancer in never smokers.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies mutagenic exposures and genomic landscapes in lung cancer among never smokers. The biological system is human lung cancer genomes. Methods include genomic sequencing and mutational signature analysis using data from the Sherlock-Lung study. The main contribution is identifying distinct mutational signatures and driver mutations associated with geographic regions and air pollution levels.

paper_summaries.title: Development of a nanoparticle-based immunotherapy targeting PD-L1 and PLK1 for lung cancer treatment.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies a nanoparticle-based immunotherapy designed to enhance PD-L1 inhibitor efficacy in non-small cell lung cancer. The biological system consists of metastatic lung tumor models (LLC-JSP and KLN-205). Methods include the use of ARAC nanoparticles co-delivering a PLK1 inhibitor and a PD-L1 antibody. The main contribution is demonstrating that ARAC selectively kills cancer cells and upregulates PD-L1, reducing effective drug doses and improving T cell-mediated tumor killing.

paper_summaries.title: A Glycemia Risk Index (GRI) of Hypoglycemia and Hyperglycemia for Continuous Glucose Monitoring Validated by Clinician Ratings.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies a composite metric for evaluating the quality of glycemia from continuous glucose monitor (CGM) data. The system involves human adults with diabetes. Methods include 14-day CGM tracings, principal component analysis, multiple regressions, and clinician rankings. The main contribution is the development and validation of the Glycemia Risk Index (GRI), a single-number summary of hypoglycemia and hyperglycemia for clinical and research use.

paper_summaries.title: Organelle Formation in Bacteria and Archaea.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the biogenesis and maintenance of lipid-bounded organelles in prokaryotes. The biological systems are bacteria and archaea. Methods are not clearly specified in the abstract. The main contribution is reviewing recent findings on prokaryotic compartmentalization using a unified definition of membrane-bounded organelles.

paper_summaries.title: Compartmentalization and organelle formation in bacteria.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies compartmentalization and organelle formation in bacteria. The biological systems discussed include Bacillus subtilis, Caulobacter crescentus, magnetosomes, and carboxysomes. Methods are not clearly specified in the abstract. The main contribution is highlighting the physical, chemical, and compositional remodeling events that lead to bacterial compartmentalization and organelle positioning.

paper_summaries.title: Bacterial actins and their diversity.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the diversity and molecular workings of bacterial actins. The biological system is the bacterial cytoskeleton. Methods are not clearly specified in the abstract. The main contribution is reviewing the functional, biochemical, and structural features of well-studied bacterial actin homologues.

paper_summaries.title: Cell biology of prokaryotic organelles.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the cell biology, ultrastructure, and molecular mechanisms of prokaryotic organelles. The biological system comprises protein-bounded and lipid-bounded organelles in prokaryotic cells. Methods are not clearly specified in the abstract. The main contribution is challenging the dogma of simple bacterial architecture by detailing the biogenesis and maintenance of complex prokaryotic organelles.

paper_summaries.title: Revealing the diversity of bacterial and archaeal organelles via comparative genomics.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the diversity of bacterial and archaeal organelles, including magnetosomes and encapsulins. The biological systems include magnetotactic bacteria, encapsulin-producing bacteria, and Asgard archaea. Methods include comparative genomics and metagenomics. The main contribution is examining how genomic approaches augment classical studies to discover and characterize the evolutionary origins and functions of microbial organelles.

paper_summaries.title: Clostridioides difficile ferrosome organelles combat nutritional immunity.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies intracellular iron biomineralization and storage in Clostridioides difficile. The biological systems are C. difficile and mouse models of infection. Methods include cryo-electron tomography and genetic knockouts. The main contribution is discovering that C. difficile forms membrane-bound ferrosome organelles using FezA and FezB to store iron and combat host nutritional immunity during infection.

paper_summaries.title: Bacterial Organelles in Iron Physiology.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies bacterial organelles involved in iron physiology and homeostasis. The biological systems include bacteria producing magnetosomes, ferrosomes, and encapsulated ferritin-like proteins. Methods are not clearly specified in the abstract. The main contribution is providing an updated overview of the genetics, biogenesis, and physiological functions of iron-containing bacterial organelles.

paper_summaries.title: Ferrous iron efflux systems in bacteria.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies ferrous iron efflux systems that protect bacteria from iron intoxication and oxidative stress. The biological system is bacteria. Methods are not clearly specified in the abstract. The main contribution is reviewing the roles of various iron export transporters, such as P1B-type ATPases and CDF proteins, in bacterial iron homeostasis.

paper_summaries.title: Bacterial hydrophilins promote pathogen desiccation tolerance.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the genetic requirements for desiccation tolerance in Acinetobacter baumannii. The biological systems include A. baumannii, a probiotic bacterium, and purified enzymes. Methods include genetic disruption, heterologous expression, and recombinant protein assays. The main contribution is identifying that the bacterial hydrophilins DtpA and DtpB promote desiccation tolerance and protect proteins from inactivation.

paper_summaries.title: FapR regulates HssRS-mediated heme homeostasis in
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the regulation of heme homeostasis in Bacillus anthracis. The biological system is Bacillus anthracis. Methods include genetic deletion of the fapR gene. The main contribution is identifying the transcriptional regulator FapR as a key factor that maintains membrane integrity, which is essential for the proper function of the HssRS heme sensing system.

paper_summaries.title: Bacterial microcompartments.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the structure, assembly, diversity, and function of bacterial microcompartments (BMCs). The biological systems are autotrophic and heterotrophic bacteria. Methods are not clearly specified in the abstract. The main contribution is reviewing recent insights into BMCs and their potential applications in synthetic biology.

paper_summaries.title: Atypical Carboxysome Loci: JEEPs or Junk?
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies atypical carboxysome loci in bacteria that lack essential structural or enzymatic genes. The biological systems are Proteobacteria and Cyanobacteria. Methods include genome sequencing analysis. The main contribution is describing these atypical loci and proposing that they function as "JEEPs" with modified roles based on the presence of just enough essential parts.

paper_summaries.title: Electrochemical cofactor recycling of bacterial microcompartments.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies electrochemical cofactor recycling within bacterial microcompartments. The biological system is bacterial microcompartments. Methods include bioinformatic analysis, functional assays, Electron Paramagnetic Resonance spectroscopy, protein voltammetry, structural modeling, and X-ray footprinting. The main contribution is identifying MNdh as an enzyme that regenerates NAD+ inside BMCs and transfers electrons outside via the BMC-TSE shell protein.

paper_summaries.title: Electrochemical cofactor recycling of bacterial microcompartments.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies electrochemical cofactor recycling in bacterial microcompartments. The biological system is bacterial microcompartments. Methods include bioinformatic analysis, functional assays, EPR spectroscopy, protein voltammetry, structural modeling, and X-ray footprinting. The main contribution is proposing NAD+ regeneration as a new function of MNdh, establishing a widely occurring route for cofactor recycling across the BMC shell.

paper_summaries.title: Engineered bacterial microcompartments: apps for programming metabolism.
paper_summaries.summary: This paper studies the genetic engineering and modification of bacterial microcompartments for biotechnological applications. The biological system is bacterial microcompartments. Methods include genetic engineering and adaptive evolution. The main contribution is highlighting the modular structure and interchangeability of BMC shell proteins, framing them as programmable metabolic apps.
